### Window Switcher[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#window-switcher "Direct link to Window Switcher")

> Shows a window switcher for the current app or all apps.

For click-and-drag switching, show the switcher on press and add **Activate Hovered Item in Window Switcher** (476) to the trigger's **On Click Release** action category. If the pointer rests on one of the switcher's shortcut buttons, 476 runs that button's action on the window the button belongs to instead of activating the keyboard selection.

On macOS 13+, a switcher action whose `BTTAdditionalActionData` contains no `BTTWindowSwitcher*` key at all is treated as unconfigured and is seeded with these defaults, both in the preferences form and when the action runs: `BTTWindowSwitcherLayout` 1, `BTTWindowSwitcherThumbnailWidth` 150, `BTTWindowSwitcherThumbnailRows` 2, `BTTWindowSwitcherWrapThumbnails` true, `BTTWindowSwitcherWidth` 800, `BTTWindowSwitcherHeight` 500, `BTTWindowSwitcherItemHeight` 30, `BTTWindowSwitcherFontSize` 12, `BTTWindowSwitcherShowPopover` 2, `BTTWindowSwitcherShowThumbnail` 1, `BTTWindowSwitcherMousePos` 3, `BTTWindowSwitcherSelectNextOnRepeat` true, `BTTWindowSwitcherTriggerOnRelease` true, `BTTWindowSwitcherVisibilityDelay` 0, `BTTWindowSwitcherCycleThroughWindowsOnly` true, `BTTWindowSwitcherAppearance` 0, `BTTWindowSwitcherSort` 0, `BTTWindowSwitcherInitialFocus` 0, `BTTWindowSwitcherFocus` 0, `BTTWindowSwitcherExclude` "", and false for every remaining boolean key. As soon as one `BTTWindowSwitcher*` key is present, nothing is seeded: the remaining missing keys keep their individual fallbacks listed below. Existing saved configurations are never migrated.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**:
    *   Current App: 99
    *   All Apps: 100
    *   Move Selection In Active Window Switcher To Previous: 378
    *   Move Selection In Active Window Switcher To Next: 693
    *   Activate Hovered: 476
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with window switcher configuration
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherShowPopover`: number - Popover display mode (0=screenshot+shortcuts, 1=screenshot only, 2=shortcuts only, 3=no popover, 4=preview of actual window, 5=preview+shortcuts, 6=shortcut buttons overlaid on the hovered thumbnail, 7=preview of actual window + overlaid shortcut buttons). Modes 6 and 7 draw the shortcut actions as icon buttons on top of the hovered card's thumbnail image instead of opening a separate popover, and they follow the mouse pointer rather than the keyboard selection. They only apply to `BTTWindowSwitcherLayout` 1 (horizontal thumbnails): with the vertical list, 6 behaves like 2 and 7 behaves like 5; in the window-previews-only layout every mode behaves like 4.
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherShowThumbnail`: number - Thumbnail mode (0=app icon, 1=window thumbnail)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherLayout`: number - Layout (0=vertical list, 1=horizontal thumbnails, 2=window previews only)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherThumbnailWidth`: number - Thumbnail width in points, 100–400 (new actions: 150; fallback for already configured actions: 200)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherThumbnailRows`: integer - Rows before scrolling, 1–10 (new actions: 2). One row scrolls horizontally; two or more wrap into a grid and scroll vertically after that many rows. Height is calculated from thumbnail width and font size, reduced to whole rows when necessary to fit the screen. Repeated triggers follow display order; Up/Down arrows move between rows.
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherWrapThumbnails`: boolean - Legacy compatibility: used only when `BTTWindowSwitcherThumbnailRows` is absent; true selects two rows, false selects one.
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherDisableMouseHover`: boolean - Disable selection by mouse hover
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherSelectNextOnRepeat`: boolean - On repeated trigger, select next window in list
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherTriggerOnRelease`: boolean - Activate selected after releasing modifier keys (requires SelectNextOnRepeat)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherVisibilityDelay`: number - Delay showing the switcher, popovers, and actual-window previews in milliseconds, clamped to 0–2000 (default/fallback: 0). Selection and keyboard handling start immediately; repeated triggers do not restart the delay. When modifier-release activation is enabled, releasing the modifiers before the delay ends activates the selection without showing the UI. Explicit activation, including Activate Hovered (476), also cancels pending presentation, even with `BTTWindowSwitcherKeepOpen` enabled. Dock hover ignores this action delay and uses the trigger's own hover delay.
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherAppearance`: number - Appearance (0=automatic, 1=light, 2=dark)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherFontSize`: number - Font size in points (default: 12)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherItemHeight`: number - Item height in pixels (vertical list only, default: 30)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherWidth`: number - Maximum width in pixels for thumbnail layouts, which shrink to fit visible windows; fixed width for the vertical list (new actions: 800; runtime fallback: 600; preferences fallback for already configured actions: 380 on macOS 13+, otherwise 600)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherHeight`: number - Height in pixels for the vertical list (new actions: 500; runtime fallback: 600; preferences fallback for already configured actions: 500); thumbnail height is automatic
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherKeepOpen`: boolean - Keep the visible switcher open after activating a window or losing focus (ignored in the window-previews-only layout). Activation or focus loss before the visibility delay ends cancels presentation instead.
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherCycleThroughWindowsOnly`: boolean - Repeated triggers and arrow keys skip the search field and cycle through windows only (new actions: true)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherMousePos`: number - Position mode (0=mouse centered left, 1=mouse left to first item, 2=mouse left to second item, 3=centered on screen with mouse, 4=centered on screen with focused window, 5=custom position)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherSort`: number - Sort order (0=last used grouped by desktop, 2=alphabetically app+window name, 3=alphabetically app+window name, 4=last used all desktops mixed)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherInitialFocus`: number - Initial focus (0=search field, 1=window list)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherHideSearchField`: boolean - Hide the search field (the window list always keeps the focus)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherFocus`: number - Selected item (0=currently active window, 1=second window in list)
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherExcludeSpecific`: boolean - Enable exclude specific apps/windows
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherExclude`: string - Exclusion filter text
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherExcludeWindowsFromOtherSpaces`: boolean - Exclude windows from other spaces
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherExcludeHiddenAndMinimizedWindows`: boolean - Exclude hidden and minimized windows
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherExcludeAllButHiddenAndMinimizedWindows`: boolean - Show only hidden and minimized windows
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherExcludeVisibleWindows`: boolean - Exclude visible windows
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherOverrideDefaultShortcuts`: boolean - Override default keyboard shortcuts
    *   `BTTWindowSwitcherAction1` through `BTTWindowSwitcherAction17`: integer - macOS virtual key codes for the switcher shortcuts, not predefined-action IDs

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 99,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTWindowSwitcherWidth": 800,    "BTTWindowSwitcherHeight": 600,    "BTTWindowSwitcherAppearance": 2,    "BTTWindowSwitcherSort": 0,    "BTTWindowSwitcherSelectNextOnRepeat": true,    "BTTWindowSwitcherTriggerOnRelease": true,    "BTTWindowSwitcherShowPopover": 4,    "BTTWindowSwitcherInitialFocus": 1  }}

*   **BTTAppToShowOrHide**: Bundle identifier or path

    *   Additional show/hide behavior settings

### Quit Specific Application[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#quit-specific-application "Direct link to Quit Specific Application")

> Quits a specific application. Supports standard quit, force quit, and an optional fallback force quit after a timeout.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 592
*   **BTTAppToQuit**: Bundle identifier or path of the app to quit
*   **BTTQuitAppConfig**: JSON string with quit configuration (optional)
    *   `BTTQuitAppForceQuit`: boolean - if true, force quits the app without allowing it to save changes
    *   `BTTQuitAppForceQuitTimeout`: number - if greater than 0 and `BTTQuitAppForceQuit` is false, BTT first requests a normal quit and force quits the same still-running app instance after the timeout in seconds

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 592,  "BTTAppToQuit": "com.apple.Safari"}

Example with force quit:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 592,  "BTTAppToQuit": "com.apple.Safari",  "BTTQuitAppConfig": "{\"BTTQuitAppForceQuit\":true}"}

Example with fallback force quit timeout:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 592,  "BTTAppToQuit": "com.apple.Safari",  "BTTQuitAppConfig": "{\"BTTQuitAppForceQuit\":false,\"BTTQuitAppForceQuitTimeout\":5}"}

### Create New File in Finder[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#create-new-file-in-finder "Direct link to Create New File in Finder")

> Creates a new file in the current Finder location and can immediately reveal and open it.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 85
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with configuration (all keys optional)
    *   `BTTCreateNewFileTarget`: string - Where to create the file: `finder` (target of the frontmost Finder window, desktop if none - default), `finderSelection` (folder selected in Finder, falls back to `finder`), `custom` (fixed folder)
    *   `BTTCreateNewFileCustomFolder`: string - Folder path, used when target is `custom` (supports ~ and placeholders)
    *   `BTTCreateNewFileNameMode`: string - `ask` (show a name dialog, prefilled with the name below - default) or `fixed` (create without asking)
    *   `BTTCreateNewFileName`: string - File name / suggested file name (default `newfile.txt`). Supports BTT variables (`{variableName}`) and date placeholders (`{date:yyyy-MM-dd}`). A `/` creates the file in a (new) subfolder.
    *   `BTTCreateNewFileContent`: string - Initial file contents, same placeholder support (default empty)
    *   `BTTCreateNewFileConflictMode`: string - If the file already exists: `unique` (create `name 2.txt` - default), `openExisting` (keep the existing file untouched), `overwrite`
    *   `BTTCreateNewFileRevealInFinder`: boolean - Select the new file in Finder (default true)
    *   `BTTCreateNewFileOpenAfterCreation`: boolean - Open the new file (default true)
    *   `BTTCreateNewFileOpenWithApp`: string - App path or bundle identifier to open the file with (default: the system default app)
    *   `BTTCreateNewFileSaveToVariable`: string - Name of a BTT variable that receives the created file path

The action returns the path of the created file, so following actions can use it.

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 85,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTCreateNewFileTarget": "finder",    "BTTCreateNewFileNameMode": "fixed",    "BTTCreateNewFileName": "Notes {date:yyyy-MM-dd}.md",    "BTTCreateNewFileContent": "# Notes\n",    "BTTCreateNewFileConflictMode": "openExisting",    "BTTCreateNewFileRevealInFinder": true,    "BTTCreateNewFileOpenAfterCreation": true  }}

### Set Audio Output Device[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#set-audio-output-device "Direct link to Set Audio Output Device")

> Changes the system audio output device. Either sets a specific device, or cycles through a user-defined list of devices. Optionally pins the selected device as the default output.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 583
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with audio device configuration
    *   `BTTAudioDeviceSwitchMode`: number - `0` = set a specific device (default), `1` = cycle through a list of devices
    *   `BTTAudioDeviceName`: string - Audio device name (mode 0)
    *   `BTTAudioDeviceUID`: string - Audio device unique identifier (mode 0)
    *   `BTTAudioDeviceCycleList`: string - one device name or UID per line (mode 1). BTT finds the current default output device in the list and switches to the next entry, wrapping around and skipping devices that are not currently connected
    *   `BTTAudioDevicePinMode`: number - `0` = don't change pinning (default), `1` = pin the selected device as default output: BTT automatically re-selects it if macOS switches to another output device (the pin is stored in the defaults key `BTTPinnedAudioOutputDeviceUID`; BTT's own "Set Audio Output Device" actions are exempt from the restore for 5 seconds), `2` = unpin

Example (specific device):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 583,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTAudioDeviceName": "MacBook Pro Speakers",    "BTTAudioDeviceUID": "BuiltInSpeakerDevice"  }}

Example (cycle through a list of devices):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 583,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTAudioDeviceSwitchMode": 1,    "BTTAudioDeviceCycleList": "MacBook Pro Speakers\nExternal Headphones"  }}

### Set Audio Input Device[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#set-audio-input-device "Direct link to Set Audio Input Device")

> Changes the system audio input device. Either sets a specific device, or cycles through a user-defined list of devices. Optionally pins the selected device as the default input.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 584
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with audio device configuration
    *   `BTTAudioDeviceSwitchMode`: number - `0` = set a specific device (default), `1` = cycle through a list of devices
    *   `BTTAudioDeviceName`: string - Audio device name (mode 0)
    *   `BTTAudioDeviceUID`: string - Audio device unique identifier (mode 0)
    *   `BTTAudioDeviceCycleList`: string - one device name or UID per line (mode 1). BTT finds the current default input device in the list and switches to the next entry, wrapping around and skipping devices that are not currently connected
    *   `BTTAudioDevicePinMode`: number - `0` = don't change pinning (default), `1` = pin the selected device as default: BTT automatically re-selects it if macOS switches to another device (the pin is stored in the defaults key `BTTPinnedAudioInputDeviceUID` for action 584 / `BTTPinnedAudioOutputDeviceUID` for action 583 - the pin option is available on BOTH the input and output device actions), `2` = unpin

Example (specific device):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 584,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTAudioDeviceName": "MacBook Pro Microphone",    "BTTAudioDeviceUID": "BuiltInMicrophoneDevice"  }}

Example (cycle through a list of devices and pin the result):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 584,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTAudioDeviceSwitchMode": 1,    "BTTAudioDeviceCycleList": "MacBook Pro Microphone\nExternal Microphone",    "BTTAudioDevicePinMode": 1  }}

### Toggle Mute Microphone (Audio Input)[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#toggle-mute-microphone-audio-input "Direct link to Toggle Mute Microphone (Audio Input)")

> Toggles the mute state of the microphone (audio input device). Optionally also sets the input volume to 0 when muting and restores it when unmuting. Can apply to all connected input devices or just the default input device.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 585
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object (optional)
    *   `BTTMicMuteAlsoSetVolume`: boolean - also set input volume to 0 when muting and restore when unmuting
    *   `BTTMicMuteApplyToAllInputDevices`: boolean - apply to all connected input devices instead of only the current default input device (coordinated mute/unmute across every input device, with read-back verification of the resulting mute state)

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 585}

Example (also set volume, apply to all input devices):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 585,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTMicMuteAlsoSetVolume": true,    "BTTMicMuteApplyToAllInputDevices": true  }}

### Play Sound File[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#play-sound-file "Direct link to Play Sound File")

> Plays a sound file.

Parameters:

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Take Screenshot[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#take-screenshot "Direct link to Take Screenshot")

> Takes a screenshot with configurable options.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 169
*   **BTTScreenshotOptions**: Screenshot configuration string (see below)
*   **BTTScreenshotDateFormat**: Date format for the `{datetime}` placeholder in the file name (optional, e.g. "yyyy-MM-dd HH.mm.ss")

The options string is a `;;`\-separated token list ending with the target file path (the path supports `{datetime}`, `{random}`, `~` and BTT variables). Tokens:

*   Capture mode (pick one):
    *   `-i`: capture interactively. Modifiers: `-U` (show toolbar), `-w` (only window selection), `-W` (start in window selection mode), `-o` (no window shadow), `-S` (capture screen instead of window)
    *   `-R;;x,y,w,h`: capture a specific screen rect (`-C` also captures the cursor)
    *   `-l;;<window id>`: capture a specific window by CG window id (`-a` excludes attached windows)
    *   Dynamic window targeting (resolved every time the action runs, same matching as action 364 "Activate Specific Window"): `BTTFindWindowTitle;;<regex>`, `BTTFindWindowApp;;<regex>`, `BTTFindWindowIndex;;<n>` (1 = topmost window, takes precedence over title/app), `BTTFindWindowFullScreenOnly`. Regex/wildcards work; BTT variables can be used inside curly braces. If nothing matches, an additional `-l;;<id>` serves as fallback, otherwise the capture is aborted.
    *   no mode token: capture whole screen(s). Modifiers: `-m` (only main monitor), `-C` (capture cursor)
*   Misc: `-x` (no sounds), `-r` (no dpi metadata), `-c` (capture only to clipboard), `-T;;<seconds>` (delay), `-t;;<png|jpg|pdf|tiff>` (file format)
*   After capture: `BTTAdditionallyCopyToClipboard` (add `BTTDontCopyPath` to copy only the image, not the file path), `BTTEditInBTT`, `BTTUploadToImgur`, `BTTRunTerminalCommand`, `-u` (default macOS screenshot UI), `-M` (new mail), `-P` (open in Preview), `-B;;<bundle id>` (open with app)

Action chaining: when the options copy the capture to the clipboard (`-c` or `BTTAdditionallyCopyToClipboard`), BTT blocks the following actions in the same sequence until the capture has finished and the clipboard change has landed (max. 2 seconds grace; a cancelled interactive capture simply continues). Follow-up actions can therefore consume the clipboard directly. Exception: if the next enabled action is "Wait For Clipboard Change" (action 499) BTT does not wait itself, so that action can detect the change.

Example (capture the frontmost Safari window):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 169,  "BTTScreenshotOptions": "BTTFindWindowApp;;Safari;;-t;;png;;~/Pictures/Screenshot_{datetime}_{random}.png;;",  "BTTScreenshotDateFormat": "yyyy-MM-dd HH.mm.ss"}

### Transform Clipboard with ChatGPT[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#transform-clipboard-with-chatgpt "Direct link to Transform Clipboard with ChatGPT")

> Transforms clipboard using ChatGPT.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 449
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with configuration
    *   `BTTChatGPTModelSelection`: Model to use ("gpt-4o-mini", "custom") - default: "gpt-4o-mini"
    *   `BTTChatGPTModel`: Custom model identifier (when using "custom" selection)
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerSystemPrompt`: System prompt for the AI
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerUserPrompt`: User prompt template - default: "Make everything uppercase, don't add any comment:"
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerExampleInput`: Example input for testing - default: "Some Test Text"
    *   `BTTChatGPTNumberOfHistoryItems`: Number of previous requests to include - default: 0
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerShowMiniHUD`: boolean - show mini HUD while waiting - default: true
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerAskWhatToDo`: boolean - always ask what to do when executing
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerCustomURL`: Custom API endpoint URL
    *   `BTTChatGPTKeepSelectedText`: boolean - keep text selected after transformation - default: true
    *   `BTTChatGPTAppendSelectedText`: boolean - append selected text to user prompt - default: true
    *   `BTTChatGPTImageFilePath`: Path to image file to attach
    *   `BTTChatGPTImageType`: Image source type (0=clipboard, 1=file)
    *   `BTTChatGPTAppendImage`: boolean - attach image to request
    *   `BTTChatGPTUseStreaming`: boolean - stream response instead of waiting - default: false for clipboard
    *   `BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToClipboard`: boolean - copy result to clipboard
    *   `BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToVariable`: boolean - save result to variable
    *   `BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToVariableName`: Variable name to store result
    *   `BTTActionPasteFormat`: Paste format options
    *   `BTTActionPasteInputFormat`: Input format for processing
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerExtraParameters`: string - Extra JSON parameters to pass to the API

Configure credentials in BTT's action preferences, which stores them in Keychain. The action JSON does not configure a credential.

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 449,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTChatGPTModelSelection": "gpt-4o-mini",    "BTTChatGPTTransformerSystemPrompt": "You are a professional translator.",    "BTTChatGPTTransformerUserPrompt": "Translate the following text to Spanish:",    "BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToClipboard": true,    "BTTChatGPTUseStreaming": true,    "BTTChatGPTTransformerShowMiniHUD": true  }}

### Wait For File Or Folder To Change[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#wait-for-file-or-folder-to-change "Direct link to Wait For File Or Folder To Change")

> Pauses an action sequence until the first matching new file or folder change is observed.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 695
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with wait configuration
    *   `BTTActionWaitForFileChangePaths`: string - Required file or folder paths, separated by `;;`. Use absolute paths or `~` for the home folder. BTT variables are resolved separately for each path when the action starts.
    *   `BTTActionWaitForFileChangeType`: integer - Change type from the table below (default: 0, any change). Uses the same values as the File Or Folder Did Change trigger's `BTTFileChangeType`.
    *   `BTTActionWaitForFileChangeTimeout`: number - Maximum wait in seconds, including setup (default: 60). `0` waits indefinitely; the maximum is `31536000` seconds (one year).
    *   `BTTActionWaitForFileChangeContinueOnTimeout`: boolean - Continue without a matching change if the timeout expires (default: false).

Existing folders include changes in their subfolders. Paths may identify files or folders that do not exist yet, including missing intermediate folders: BTT watches the nearest existing parent for their creation. An item that already exists when monitoring begins does not satisfy a creation wait. Use a narrower folder or specific files for very large folder trees.

macOS can combine several filesystem operations into one event. A matching event reports a change; the producing app may still be writing the file. Observations use a bounded initial inventory (100,000 items, up to 10 seconds) and report an error if the folder cannot be inspected reliably or macOS reports lost events. Ancestor symlinks are resolved; a selected symlink is watched as a link, and symlinks inside a folder are not traversed.

Change types:

| Configuration value | Change | Result variable value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0   | Any change | Actual change type below |
| 1   | Directory created | 0   |
| 2   | Directory removed | 1   |
| 3   | Directory renamed | 2   |
| 4   | Directory modified | 3   |
| 5   | File created | 4   |
| 6   | File removed | 5   |
| 7   | File renamed / moved into folder | 6   |
| 8   | File modified | 7   |
| 9   | File moved out of folder | 8   |

Result variables:

*   **BTTFileChangeWaitResult**: `changed`, `timeout`, `cancelled`, or `error`.
*   **BTTFileChangeWaitError**: Error description for `error`; empty for the other results.
*   **BTTLastChangedFileOrFolder**: Matching path, updated only when the result is `changed`.
*   **BTTLastChangedFileOrFolderChangedType**: Zero-based change type from the table, matching the trigger's result variable; `-1` means unknown. Updated only when the result is `changed`.

A matching change continues the sequence once. By default, a timeout stops the enclosing action sequence, including actions after an enclosing End If or End Repeat. Enabling `BTTActionWaitForFileChangeContinueOnTimeout` allows continuation on timeout. Invalid configuration or monitoring errors stop the enclosing sequence regardless of this setting.

Stop All Running Action Sequences cancels active file waits. Cancel Repeat cancels file waits within the selected repeat loop and preserves its usual continuation after End Repeat. The last changed path and type retain their previous values after timeout, cancellation, or error; check `BTTFileChangeWaitResult` when using timeout continuation.

Example (wait up to 30 seconds for a new file at either path):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 695,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionWaitForFileChangePaths": "~/Downloads/report.csv;;~/Exports/ready.json",    "BTTActionWaitForFileChangeType": 5,    "BTTActionWaitForFileChangeTimeout": 30,    "BTTActionWaitForFileChangeContinueOnTimeout": false  }}

### Change Formatting of Selected Text[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#change-formatting-of-selected-text "Direct link to Change Formatting of Selected Text")

> Changes formatting of selected text with extensive customization options.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 494
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with formatting configuration
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingSetFontSize`: boolean - Set specific font size
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingFontSizeFix`: number - Fixed font size to set (when SetFontSize is true)
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingChangeFontSize`: boolean - Change font size relatively
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingFontSizeChange`: number - Font size change amount (positive/negative)
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingChangeFontColor`: boolean - Change font color
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingFontColor`: string - Font color (hex format, e.g., "#FF0000")
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingChangeBackgroundColor`: boolean - Change background color
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingBackgroundColor`: string - Background color (hex format)
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingUseTemplateString`: boolean - Use template string for advanced formatting
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingTemplateString`: string - Template string with placeholders
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingIgnoreFontSize`: boolean - Preserve original font size
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingIgnoreFont`: boolean - Preserve original font
    *   `BTTActionChangeTextFormattingIgnoreAlignment`: boolean - Preserve original alignment

Example (Set fixed font size):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 494,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionChangeTextFormattingSetFontSize": true,    "BTTActionChangeTextFormattingFontSizeFix": 16  }}

Example (Change font size relatively):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 494,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionChangeTextFormattingChangeFontSize": true,    "BTTActionChangeTextFormattingFontSizeChange": 2  }}

Example (Change colors):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 494,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionChangeTextFormattingChangeFontColor": true,    "BTTActionChangeTextFormattingFontColor": "#FF0000",    "BTTActionChangeTextFormattingChangeBackgroundColor": true,    "BTTActionChangeTextFormattingBackgroundColor": "#FFFF00"  }}

Example (Use template string):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 494,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionChangeTextFormattingUseTemplateString": true,    "BTTActionChangeTextFormattingTemplateString": "**{{text}}**",    "BTTActionChangeTextFormattingIgnoreFont": true  }}

### Transform Selected Text with ChatGPT[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#transform-selected-text-with-chatgpt "Direct link to Transform Selected Text with ChatGPT")

> Transforms selected text using ChatGPT.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 384
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with configuration - same keys as Transform Clipboard with ChatGPT
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerSystemPrompt`: string - System prompt for the AI
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerUserPrompt`: string - User prompt template
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerExampleInput`: string - Example input for testing
    *   `BTTChatGPTModelSelection`: string - Model to use ("custom" enables the custom model fields)
    *   `BTTChatGPTModel`: string - Custom model identifier (only used when BTTChatGPTModelSelection is "custom")
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerCustomURL`: string - Custom API endpoint URL
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerExtraParameters`: string - Extra JSON parameters to pass to the API, e.g. temperature (only used when BTTChatGPTModelSelection is "custom")
    *   `BTTChatGPTNumberOfHistoryItems`: number - Number of previous requests to include
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerShowMiniHUD`: boolean - Show a mini HUD while waiting
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerAskWhatToDo`: boolean - Always ask what to do
    *   `BTTChatGPTKeepSelectedText`: boolean - Keep the text selected
    *   `BTTChatGPTAppendSelectedText`: boolean - Append the selected text to the prompt
    *   `BTTChatGPTAppendImage`: boolean - Attach an image to the request
    *   `BTTChatGPTImageType`: number - Image source type (only used when BTTChatGPTAppendImage is true)
    *   `BTTChatGPTImageFilePath`: string - Path to the image file to attach (only used when BTTChatGPTAppendImage is true and BTTChatGPTImageType is 1)
    *   `BTTChatGPTUseStreaming`: boolean - Stream the response
    *   `BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToClipboard`: boolean - Copy the result to the clipboard
    *   `BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToVariable`: boolean - Save the result to a variable
    *   `BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToVariableName`: string - Variable name to store the result (only used when BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToVariable is true)
    *   `BTTActionPasteFormat`: string - Paste format options
    *   `BTTActionPasteInputFormat`: string - Input format for processing
*   The OpenAI/compatible API key is stored in the macOS Keychain (configured through the BTT UI), not in the trigger JSON.

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 384,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTChatGPTTransformerSystemPrompt": "You are a professional editor.",    "BTTChatGPTTransformerUserPrompt": "Fix grammar and spelling.",    "BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToClipboard": true,    "BTTChatGPTUseStreaming": true  }}

### ChatGPT Selection to Clipboard & Variable[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#chatgpt-selection-to-clipboard--variable "Direct link to ChatGPT Selection to Clipboard & Variable")

> Processes selection with ChatGPT, saves to clipboard and variable.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 471
*   **BTTVariableName**: Variable to save result (deprecated - use BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToVariableName)
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with configuration - same keys as other ChatGPT actions
    *   `BTTChatGPTModelSelection`: Model to use ("gpt-4o-mini", "custom")
    *   `BTTChatGPTModel`: Custom model identifier
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerSystemPrompt`: System prompt
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerUserPrompt`: User prompt template
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerExampleInput`: Example input
    *   `BTTChatGPTNumberOfHistoryItems`: History items to include
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerShowMiniHUD`: boolean - show mini HUD
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerAskWhatToDo`: boolean - ask what to do
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerCustomURL`: Custom API URL
    *   `BTTChatGPTKeepSelectedText`: boolean - keep selected
    *   `BTTChatGPTAppendSelectedText`: boolean - append selected text
    *   `BTTChatGPTImageFilePath`: Image file path
    *   `BTTChatGPTImageType`: Image source (0=clipboard, 1=file)
    *   `BTTChatGPTAppendImage`: boolean - attach image
    *   `BTTChatGPTUseStreaming`: boolean - stream response
    *   `BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToClipboard`: boolean - copy to clipboard - default: true
    *   `BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToVariable`: boolean - save to variable - default: true
    *   `BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToVariableName`: Variable name - default: "BTTChatGPTResponse"
    *   `BTTActionPasteFormat`: Paste format
    *   `BTTActionPasteInputFormat`: Input format
    *   `BTTChatGPTTransformerExtraParameters`: string - Extra JSON parameters to pass to the API

Configure credentials in BTT's action preferences, which stores them in Keychain. The action JSON does not configure a credential.

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 471,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTChatGPTModelSelection": "gpt-4o-mini",    "BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToClipboard": true,    "BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToVariable": true,    "BTTChatGPTCopyResponseToVariableName": "summary",    "BTTChatGPTUseStreaming": true  }}

### OCR (Extract Text from Image)[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#ocr-extract-text-from-image "Direct link to OCR (Extract Text from Image)")

> Recognizes text in an image from the clipboard or a file. Action 498 does not capture a screen area itself; capture an image first when that is needed. QR / matrix barcode payloads (QR, Micro QR, Aztec, Data Matrix, PDF417) are appended to the recognized text by default. Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 498
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with OCR configuration
    *   `BTTOCRSourceType`: number - Source type (0=clipboard, 1=file)
    *   `BTTOCRFileAtPath`: string - Path to image file (when sourceType=1)
    *   `BTTOCRAutoDetectLanguage`: boolean - Auto-detect language
    *   `BTTOCRLanguages`: string - Comma-separated language codes (e.g., `"en-US,de-DE"`)
    *   `BTTOCRCustomWords`: string - Comma-separated custom words for recognition
    *   `BTTOCRJoinBasedOnScreenCoordinates`: boolean - Join text based on position
    *   `BTTOCRJoinFoundStringsWithCharacter`: string - Character to join text (e.g., " " or "\\n")
    *   `BTTOCRSaveToVariable`: string - Variable name to save result
    *   `BTTOCRCopyToClipboard`: boolean - Copy result to clipboard
    *   `BTTOCRDetectQRCodes`: boolean - Append QR / matrix barcode payloads (QR, Micro QR, Aztec, Data Matrix, PDF417) to the recognized text (default: true, set to false to disable) Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 498,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTOCRSourceType": 0,    "BTTOCRAutoDetectLanguage": true,    "BTTOCRCopyToClipboard": true,    "BTTOCRSaveToVariable": "ocr_result"  }}

### Find Text on Screen[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#find-text-on-screen "Direct link to Find Text on Screen")

> Runs OCR on the selected screen area, looks for the configured text and optionally moves the mouse to the match and runs named triggers.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 426
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig2**: string - the search configuration as a **JSON string** (a nested JSON object is not accepted for this action). It holds the following keys:
    *   `BTTFindText`: string - the text to search for. BTT variables inside the string are resolved before searching
    *   `BTTFindTextMatchMode`: number - how the text is compared against each recognized string: 1 = contains (default), 2 = begins with, 3 = ends with, 4 = equals, 5 = matches (regex)
    *   `BTTFindTextSearchDirection`: number - order in which matches are sorted: 0 = left to right, then top to bottom; 1 = top to bottom, then left to right
    *   `BTTFindTextRequiredOccurences`: number - which occurrence to use: 0 = the first match, n = the n-th match (1-based). If fewer matches are recognized, the search counts as failed
    *   `BTTFindTextSearchOn`: number - which area is captured: 0 = all screens, 1 = screen with mouse cursor, 2 = main screen, 3 = screens without the mouse cursor, 4 = screen containing the focused window, 5 = only the focused window
    *   `BTTFindTextSearchRegion`: number - restricts the captured area: 0 = whole area, 1-4 = quarters, 5/6 = top/bottom half, 7/8 = left/right half
    *   `BTTFindTextMoveMouseTo`: number - 0 = do not move the mouse; any non-zero value moves the mouse to the matched text
    *   `BTTFindTextIfFoundTrigger`: string - name of a named trigger to run when the text was found
    *   `BTTFindTextIfNotFoundTrigger`: string - name of a named trigger to run when the text was not found
    *   `BTTFindTextContinueActionExecution`: boolean - if true, the remaining actions still run when the text was not found

After execution, the following BTT variables are set:

*   `last_find_text_on_screen_result`: JSON string with `recognizedText` and `boundingRects` arrays (empty string if no match)
*   `last_find_text_on_screen_success`: `1` if the text was found (also `1` if not found but `BTTFindTextContinueActionExecution` is enabled), `0` otherwise

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 426,  "BTTGenericActionConfig2": "{\"BTTFindText\":\"Submit\",\"BTTFindTextMatchMode\":1,\"BTTFindTextSearchOn\":1,\"BTTFindTextMoveMouseTo\":1,\"BTTFindTextIfFoundTrigger\":\"Click Submit\"}"}

### Run Core JavaScript[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#run-core-javascript "Direct link to Run Core JavaScript")

> Executes Core JavaScript code (BTT's built-in JS engine with async/await support). Set `BTTScriptFunctionToCall` in BTTAdditionalActionData to the name of the (async) function BTT should call; its return value is the action result (returned by trigger\_named / trigger\_action). Without it the script is only evaluated and must call `returnToBTT(value)` itself.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 281
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: Object with:
    *   **BTTAppleScriptString**: JavaScript code
    *   **BTTScriptType**: 3
    *   **BTTAppleScriptRunInBackground**: true
    *   **BTTAppleScriptUsePath**: false
    *   **BTTScriptLocation**: 0

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 281,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTScriptType": 3,    "BTTAppleScriptUsePath": false,    "BTTScriptLocation": 0,    "BTTAppleScriptRunInBackground": true,    "BTTAppleScriptString": "let result = await callBTT('trigger_named', {trigger_name: 'MyTrigger'}); returnToBTT(result);"  }}

### Run JavaScript in Browser[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#run-javascript-in-browser "Direct link to Run JavaScript in Browser")

> Evaluates JavaScript directly in the active tab of a web browser and returns the result. Uses the BetterTouchTool Safari/Chrome browser extension when available. If no matching extension is active, BTT falls back to browser scripting for Safari and Chromium based browsers. Use an async IIFE if you need `await`. Only Safari and Chromium based browsers are supported.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 600
*   **BTTLaunchPath**: The JavaScript to evaluate in the active browser tab (default: `document.title`)
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with configuration (optional)
    *   `BTTActionRunJavaScriptInBrowserTarget`: string - Which browser to target. Use `"focusedBrowser"` (default) to run in the currently focused browser, or a specific browser bundle identifier. Supported bundle identifiers:
        *   `"com.apple.Safari"` - Safari
        *   `"com.google.Chrome"` - Google Chrome
        *   `"com.google.Chrome.beta"` - Google Chrome Beta
        *   `"com.google.Chrome.dev"` - Google Chrome Dev
        *   `"com.google.Chrome.canary"` - Google Chrome Canary
        *   `"com.microsoft.edgemac"` - Microsoft Edge
        *   `"com.brave.Browser"` - Brave Browser
        *   `"com.vivaldi.Vivaldi"` - Vivaldi
        *   `"company.thebrowser.Browser"` - Arc
        *   `"com.operasoftware.Opera"` - Opera
        *   `"org.chromium.Chromium"` - Chromium

Example (run in the currently focused browser):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 600,  "BTTLaunchPath": "document.title",  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionRunJavaScriptInBrowserTarget": "focusedBrowser"  }}

Example (target Google Chrome specifically, with an async IIFE):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 600,  "BTTLaunchPath": "(async () => { const r = await fetch('https://example.com'); return r.status; })()",  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionRunJavaScriptInBrowserTarget": "com.google.Chrome"  }}

### Trigger Named Trigger[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#trigger-named-trigger "Direct link to Trigger Named Trigger")

> Executes a named trigger by name. If the named trigger declares variables, values for them can be passed along.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 248
*   **BTTNamedTriggerToTrigger**: Trigger name
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: Optional object with one `BTTActionTriggerNamedTriggerVar_<variableName>` entry per variable declared by the target named trigger. The values are set as BTT variables right before the named trigger runs and may contain `{variableName}` placeholders. Entries for variables the target named trigger does not declare, and entries with an empty value, are ignored. Values are always written here as strings; a variable the named trigger declares with `BTTNamedTriggerAIVar1Type` / `BTTNamedTriggerAIVar2Type` set to 1 (at most two variables can be declared, in the named trigger's own configuration) is stored as a number variable instead of a text variable.

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 248,  "BTTNamedTriggerToTrigger": "My Custom Action",  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionTriggerNamedTriggerVar_mode": "dark"  }}

### Switch Stream Deck Plugin Profile[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#switch-stream-deck-plugin-profile "Direct link to Switch Stream Deck Plugin Profile")

> Switches the Stream Deck plugin to a different profile. Bundled starter profiles are available for all supported BTT Stream Deck plugin device types, and the amount is configurable when installing the BTT Stream Deck plugin. Leave the profile name empty to return to the previous profile. An optional page number (1-based) can be specified to jump directly to a specific page within the profile. If no target device serial is specified, BetterTouchTool switches all connected Stream Deck plugin devices. Legacy names such as `BTT Main` and `BTT Focus` are still recognized and mapped to the numbered starter profiles.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 593
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig**: Profile name to switch to (empty = return to previous profile)
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object
    *   `BTTStreamDeckPluginTargetDeviceSerial`: Optional target Stream Deck serial number (empty = switch all connected plugin devices)
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig2**: Optional page number (1-based)

Bundled starter profiles use numbered names such as:

*   BTT-01
*   BTT-02
*   BTT-03
*   BTT-04
*   BTT-05
*   BTT-06
*   BTT-07
*   BTT-08

If you install more bundled profiles, the numbering simply continues (`BTT-09`, `BTT-10`, etc.).

Example (switch to a named profile):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 593,  "BTTGenericActionConfig": "BTT-03"}

Example (switch to profile page 2):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 593,  "BTTGenericActionConfig": "BTT-05",  "BTTGenericActionConfig2": "2"}

Example (switch only one connected Stream Deck):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 593,  "BTTGenericActionConfig": "BTT-07",  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTStreamDeckPluginTargetDeviceSerial": "fc636d61da59e05b74d0120a0c917418"  }}

Example (return to previous profile):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 593}

### Macro Pad: Change / Set Brightness[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#macro-pad-change--set-brightness "Direct link to Macro Pad: Change / Set Brightness")

> Changes (relative) or sets (absolute) the brightness of connected macro pad devices. These actions are hardware-agnostic: they drive Elgato Stream Deck devices as well as the Mirabox / AJAZZ "Stream Dock" family (AKP03, AKP05E, AKP153, M18 and rebadges) and Loupedeck / Razer Stream Controller devices. The action IDs are unchanged - only the displayed names were updated from "Stream Deck: Change/Set Brightness" to "Macro Pad: Change/Set Brightness". Non-Elgato macro pads require macOS 13.0 or later.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**:
    *   Change Brightness: 343
    *   Set Brightness: 344
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig**: Brightness value (0-100 for set, +/- delta for change)
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig2**: Optional device filter. Empty = all connected devices. Accepts a device serial number, `model:<modelKey>` to target every device of one model, or `family:<familyKey>` to target a whole brand (`elgato`, `elgato-plugin-mode`, `mirabox`, `loupedeck`) - the same syntax the floating menu macro pad bindings use. The `model:` / `family:` forms select non-Elgato pads (Mirabox / AJAZZ, Loupedeck); Elgato Stream Decks are matched by serial number for this action.

Example (set all connected devices to 75%):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 344,  "BTTGenericActionConfig": "75"}

Example (dim one specific device by 10%):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 343,  "BTTGenericActionConfig": "-10",  "BTTGenericActionConfig2": "AL12K1A00567"}

### Macro Pad: Turn Off / Turn On / Toggle[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#macro-pad-turn-off--turn-on--toggle "Direct link to Macro Pad: Turn Off / Turn On / Toggle")

> Turns connected macro pad devices off or on, or toggles them. Like the brightness actions these are hardware-agnostic and cover Elgato Stream Deck devices as well as the Mirabox / AJAZZ "Stream Dock" family and Loupedeck / Razer Stream Controller devices. The action IDs are unchanged - only the displayed names were updated from "Turn Stream Deck Off/On" and "Toggle Stream Deck On/Off" to "Macro Pad: Turn Off / Turn On / Toggle On/Off". On Mirabox/AJAZZ and Loupedeck hardware there is no separate power switch: "off" sets the panel brightness to 0 and "on" restores the brightness that was used before. Non-Elgato macro pads require macOS 13.0 or later.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**:
    *   Turn Off: 347
    *   Turn On: 348
    *   Toggle On/Off: 349
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig**: Optional device filter. Empty = all connected devices. Accepts a device serial number, `model:<modelKey>` to target every device of one model, or `family:<familyKey>` to target a whole brand (`elgato`, `elgato-plugin-mode`, `mirabox`, `loupedeck`). The `model:` / `family:` forms select non-Elgato pads (Mirabox / AJAZZ, Loupedeck); Elgato Stream Decks are matched by serial number for this action.

Example (toggle all connected devices):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 349}

Example (turn off one specific device):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 347,  "BTTGenericActionConfig": "AL12K1A00567"}

### Show/Hide Stream Deck Emulator[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#showhide-stream-deck-emulator "Direct link to Show/Hide Stream Deck Emulator")

Floating Menu Actions[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#floating-menu-actions "Direct link to Floating Menu Actions")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Show Floating Menu[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#show-floating-menu "Direct link to Show Floating Menu")

> Shows a specific floating menu.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 386
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with menu configuration
    *   `BTTMenuActionMenuID`: Menu UUID or identifier (primary way to specify the menu). Can be omitted when this action is a menu-level trigger child of a floating menu (`BTTActionCategory` 50) - it then targets its owning menu
    *   `BTTMenuActionMenuName`: Menu name (alternative to UUID, for display/lookup)
    *   `BTTMenuActionActivateKeyboardFocus`: Keyboard focus mode (0 = do NOT steal keyboard focus, 1 = activate window & steal keyboard focus, 2 = steal keyboard focus without activating window)
    *   `BTTMenuActionHideOnModifierRelease`: boolean - hide the menu after releasing all pressed modifier keys
    *   `BTTMenuActionRestorePosition`: boolean - always move & resize to defined position when showing (defaults to true)
    *   `BTTMenuActionTriggerHoveredOnHide`: boolean - trigger hovered item when menu is being hidden
    *   `BTTMenuActionCloseSubmenuOnHide`: boolean - close submenus when menu is being hidden

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 386,  "BTTPredefinedActionName": "Show Floating Menu",  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTMenuActionMenuName": "Move Window to Space",    "BTTMenuActionActivateKeyboardFocus": 0,    "BTTMenuActionHideOnModifierRelease": 0,    "BTTMenuActionRestorePosition": true,    "BTTMenuActionTriggerHoveredOnHide": 0,    "BTTMenuActionCloseSubmenuOnHide": 0  }}

### Hide Floating Menu[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#hide-floating-menu "Direct link to Hide Floating Menu")

> Hides a specific floating menu.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 387
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with menu configuration
    *   `BTTMenuActionMenuID`: Menu UUID or identifier. Can be omitted when this action is a menu-level trigger child of a floating menu (`BTTActionCategory` 50) - it then targets its owning menu
    *   `BTTMenuActionMenuName`: Menu name (alternative to UUID)
    *   `BTTMenuActionTriggerHoveredOnHide`: boolean - trigger hovered item when menu is being hidden
    *   `BTTMenuActionCloseSubmenuOnHide`: boolean - close submenus when menu is being hidden
    *   `BTTMenuActionReleaseFromMemory`: boolean - close the menu and release its content (including cached web views) from memory instead of only hiding it. Overrides the menu's "Keep Menu In Cache" / "Keep Active In Background" settings - the menu and its web content are recreated the next time it is shown

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 387,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTMenuActionMenuName": "QuickActions",    "BTTMenuActionTriggerHoveredOnHide": 0,    "BTTMenuActionCloseSubmenuOnHide": 0,    "BTTMenuActionReleaseFromMemory": 0  }}

### Toggle Floating Menu[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#toggle-floating-menu "Direct link to Toggle Floating Menu")

> Toggles visibility of floating menu.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 388
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with menu configuration
    *   `BTTMenuActionMenuID`: Menu UUID or identifier. Can be omitted when this action is a menu-level trigger child of a floating menu (`BTTActionCategory` 50) - it then targets its owning menu
    *   `BTTMenuActionMenuName`: Menu name (alternative to UUID)
    *   `BTTMenuActionActivateKeyboardFocus`: Keyboard focus mode (0 = don't steal, 1 = activate window & steal, 2 = steal without activating)
    *   `BTTMenuActionHideOnModifierRelease`: boolean - hide after releasing all pressed modifier keys
    *   `BTTMenuActionRestorePosition`: boolean - always move & resize to defined position when showing (defaults to true)
    *   `BTTMenuActionTriggerHoveredOnHide`: boolean - trigger hovered item when menu is being hidden
    *   `BTTMenuActionCloseSubmenuOnHide`: boolean - close submenus when menu is being hidden

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 388,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTMenuActionMenuName": "QuickActions",    "BTTMenuActionActivateKeyboardFocus": 0,    "BTTMenuActionRestorePosition": true  }}

### Open Floating Menu Submenu[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#open-floating-menu-submenu "Direct link to Open Floating Menu Submenu")

> Opens a submenu in floating menu. You can specify the target either by item UUID, or by menu name + item name. It also enters that submenu on macro pads driven by a floating menu (macOS 13.0+); the optional `BTTMenuActionMacroPadDevice` key limits this to one pad (empty = all such pads, otherwise a device serial number, `model:<modelKey>` for every device of one model, or `family:<familyKey>` for a whole brand - `elgato`, `elgato-plugin-mode`, `mirabox`, `loupedeck`).

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 472
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with submenu configuration
    *   `BTTMenuActionMenuItemUUID`: UUID of the menu item (right-click item in BTT to copy UUID)
    *   `BTTMenuActionMenuName`: Menu name to find the item in
    *   `BTTMenuActionMenuItemName`: Item name within the menu

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 472,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTMenuActionMenuName": "MainMenu",    "BTTMenuActionMenuItemName": "FileSubmenu"  }}

### Close Floating Menu Submenu[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#close-floating-menu-submenu "Direct link to Close Floating Menu Submenu")

> Closes current floating menu submenu. You can optionally provide the parent menu name or UUID. If no identifier is provided, all open submenus will be closed. It also leaves the current submenu on macro pads driven by a floating menu (macOS 13.0+); the optional `BTTMenuActionMacroPadDevice` key limits this to one pad (empty = all such pads, otherwise a device serial number, `model:<modelKey>` for every device of one model, or `family:<familyKey>` for a whole brand - `elgato`, `elgato-plugin-mode`, `mirabox`, `loupedeck`).

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 445

Example:

Control Flow Actions[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#control-flow-actions "Direct link to Control Flow Actions")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Delay (Async / Non-Blocking)[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#delay-async--non-blocking "Direct link to Delay (Async / Non-Blocking)")

> This action pauses the execution of the current action sequence but allows the BTT process to continue processing other stuff. Usually you'd use this action to add some delays to your action sequences, e.g. when waiting for some UI to react. If you need longer timeouts (e.g. to trigger something after 10 minutes) use the "Trigger Action Sequence After Timeout" action instead.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 345
*   **BTTDelayNextActionBy**: The amount of time to pause the action execution. Provided as number with a dot as decimal separator.

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 345,  "BTTDelayNextActionBy": 2.5}

### Delay (Blocking)[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#delay-blocking "Direct link to Delay (Blocking)")

> This one freezes the BTT process for the specified amount of time, preventing any action processing during that time. You should only ever use this with small delays.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 129
*   **BTTDelayNextActionBy**: The amount of time to freeze / block the action execution. Provided as number with a dot as decimal separator.

**Note**: Usually you should use the "Delay (Async / Non-Blocking) action instead. The blocking one is only helpful for very few usecases.

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 129,  "BTTDelayNextActionBy": 2.5}

### Start Repeat[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#start-repeat "Direct link to Start Repeat")

> This marks the start of a for loop / repeat. All actions that come between this and the "End / Stop Repeat" action will be repeated.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 329
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig**: The name of the for loop (used by "Cancel Repeat" and as the variable name that holds the current iteration index)
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: Contains further action configuration object
    *   `BTTActionForLoopRepeat`: Number of times the for loop should repeat (number)
    *   `BTTActionForLoopRepeatVariable`: If the number of repeats is controlled by a BTT variable, you can specify the variable here (the variable's value is read when the loop starts and takes precedence over `BTTActionForLoopRepeat`)

**Notes**:

*   A repeat count of 0 (or a missing / invalid count) does not run the loop body at all; execution continues after the matching "End / Stop Repeat".
*   Loops can be nested. Every "Start Repeat" needs a matching "End / Stop Repeat" on the same level.

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 329,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionForLoopRepeat": 99  },  "BTTGenericActionConfig": "nameOfTheLoop"}

### End / Stop Repeat[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#end--stop-repeat "Direct link to End / Stop Repeat")

> Marks the end of the repeat / for loop.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 332

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 332}

### Break[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#break "Direct link to Break")

> Can only be used between "Start Repeat" and "End/Stop Repeat". Behaves like a standard break e.g. in JavaScript: the rest of the current iteration is skipped, the loop ends and execution continues after the matching "End / Stop Repeat". With nested loops it breaks the innermost loop the Break action is placed in.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 331

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 331}

### Cancel Repeat[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#cancel-repeat "Direct link to Cancel Repeat")

> This will cancel the specified repeat loop (if it is running). Like "Break", the rest of the current iteration of that loop is skipped and the sequence continues after the loop's "End / Stop Repeat". Can also be used from a different trigger / action sequence than the loop itself.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 424
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig**: The name of the repeat / loop that shall be canceled (the `BTTGenericActionConfig` of the "Start Repeat" action).

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 424,  "BTTGenericActionConfig": "theLoopIdentifier"}

### IF Condition[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#if-condition "Direct link to IF Condition")

> Starts conditional block based on variable.

**How If blocks work** (applies to all IF actions: 330, 431, 405, 428): the actions after the IF up to the matching "ELSE" (or "END IF" if there is no else) run when the condition is true, the actions between "ELSE" and "END IF" run when it is false. Afterwards the sequence continues after the matching "END IF". If blocks can be nested and can be placed inside repeat loops. Every IF should have a matching "END IF" on the same level. If an IF has no matching "END IF" (legacy structures, e.g. an else-if chain closed by a single "END IF" or none at all), BTT falls back to the pre-6.727 behavior: the If block simply runs to the end of the action list, and the "ELSE" branch is collected starting at the first "ELSE" encountered regardless of nesting (so the "ELSE" of an unclosed nested IF acts as the outer else). Always generate balanced IF / END IF pairs; the fallback only exists so old presets keep working. Only the first "ELSE" on a level is honoured; the actions after a second "ELSE" on the same level never run.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 330
*   **BTTIfConditionFormat**: Condition format string
*   **BTTIfConditionData**: Condition data (base64 encoded)

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 330,  "BTTIfConditionFormat": "myVar == 'true'",  "BTTIfConditionData": "base64_encoded_data"}

### IF JavaScript True[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#if-javascript-true "Direct link to IF JavaScript True")

> Conditional based on JavaScript evaluation (BTT's built-in Core JavaScript engine, same as "Run Core JavaScript"). The script is evaluated asynchronously; the If block continues once the script has delivered its result. Booleans and the strings "true" / "false" are accepted, anything else counts as false.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 431
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: Object with:
    *   **BTTAppleScriptString**: The JavaScript code
    *   **BTTScriptFunctionToCall**: Name of the (async) function in the script that BTT calls; its return value is the condition result. If omitted, the script itself must hand the result back via `returnToBTT(true)` / `returnToBTT(false)`.
    *   **BTTScriptType**: 3
    *   **BTTActionJSRunInSeparateContext**: true to run in a separate JS context instead of the shared global one (optional)

**Note**: There is no "IF AppleScript True" action (type 432 exists internally but was never implemented and is not selectable). To use an AppleScript condition, run the AppleScript from within this JavaScript action (e.g. via `runAppleScript`) and return its result.

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 431,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTScriptType": 3,    "BTTScriptFunctionToCall": "someJavaScriptFunction",    "BTTAppleScriptString": "async function someJavaScriptFunction() {\n  let clipboard = await callBTT('get_clipboard_content', {});\n  return clipboard.length > 0;\n}"  }}

### IF Image Visible[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#if-image-visible "Direct link to IF Image Visible")

> Conditional based on image visibility on screen.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 405
*   **BTTFindPositionOfImageImage**: Base64 encoded image
*   **BTTFindPositionOfImageImageDark**: Base64 encoded dark mode image (optional)

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 405,  "BTTFindPositionOfImageImage": "base64_image_data"}

### IF Text Visible[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#if-text-visible "Direct link to IF Text Visible")

> Conditional based on text visibility on screen.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 428
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig**: Text to find

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 428,  "BTTGenericActionConfig": "Submit Button"}

### ELSE[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#else "Direct link to ELSE")

> Else clause for IF conditions. Optional; only the first ELSE on a level is honoured (actions after a second ELSE on the same level never run).

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 333

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 333}

### END IF[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#end-if "Direct link to END IF")

> Ends conditional block. Every IF action should have a matching END IF on the same level; an IF without one runs to the end of the action list (legacy fallback, see "How If blocks work" above). A missing END IF is shown as a hint in the action list, while a missing "End / Stop Repeat" is a warning because the whole rest of the list would loop.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 334

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 334}

### Execute Action Sequence After Timeout (Cancellable)[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#execute-action-sequence-after-timeout-cancellable "Direct link to Execute Action Sequence After Timeout (Cancellable)")

> This allows to execute an action sequence after a specific amount of time. While the previously described delay actions are only meant to be used for short delays, this one can also be used for longer delays. Additionally you can specify a name for the timer, which allows you to cancel it if necessary.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 351
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig**: The timeout in seconds as string using a dot as decimal separator
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig2**: The name of the timer
*   **BTTAdditionalActions**: An array of actions that shall be executed after the timeout

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 351,  "BTTGenericActionConfig2": "timerName",  "BTTGenericActionConfig": "3.5",  "BTTAdditionalActions": [    {      "BTTTriggerType": 740,      "BTTPredefinedActionType": 366,      "BTTTriggerClass": "BTTTriggerTypeCustomActionConfig",      "BTTAdditionalActions": [        {          "BTTTriggerClass": "BTTTriggerTypeCustomActionConfig",          "BTTPredefinedActionType": 3        },        {          "BTTTriggerClass": "BTTTriggerTypeCustomActionConfig",          "BTTPredefinedActionType": 3        }      ]    }  ]}

### Cancel Timed / Delayed Action Sequences[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#cancel-timed--delayed-action-sequences "Direct link to Cancel Timed / Delayed Action Sequences")

> Cancels the execution of action sequences that has been scheduled via predefined action "Execute Action Sequence After Timeout (Cancellable)".

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 352
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig2**: The name of the scheduled action sequence you want to cancel

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 352,  "BTTGenericActionConfig2": "theNameOfTheTimer"}

### Ask For Input & Save To Variable[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#ask-for-input--save-to-variable "Direct link to Ask For Input & Save To Variable")

> Shows a floating input field and saves the entered text into a variable.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 403
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: Contains the configuration object
    *   `BTTActionAskForInputPrompt`: The input prompt (string)
    *   `BTTActionAskForInputVariableName`: The variable name (string)
    *   `BTTActionAskForInputVariableType`: 0 - String or 1 Number
    *   `BTTActionAskForInputOnlyHideOnEnterOrEsc`: 0: Hide when clicking outside, when hitting esc or when hitting enter. 1: Hide when hitting esc or when hitting enter

Example:

### Wait for Conditions To Become True[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#wait-for-conditions-to-become-true "Direct link to Wait for Conditions To Become True")

*   **BTTGenericActionConfig**: An identifier to reference the wait
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig2**: A JSON string with the properties BTTActionWaitForConditionsInterval and BTTActionWaitForConditionsTimeout

Example:

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 567
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig**: UUID of the trigger to wait for
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with configuration
    *   `BTTActionWaitForTriggerTimeout`: number - Timeout in seconds (default: very large value)

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 567,  "BTTGenericActionConfig": "12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012",  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionWaitForTriggerTimeout": 30  }}

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 579
*   **BTTGenericActionConfig**: Debounce time in seconds (as string)

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 579,  "BTTGenericActionConfig": "2.0"}

### Set Variable[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#set-variable "Direct link to Set Variable")

### Cycle Through Multiple Actions[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#cycle-through-multiple-actions "Direct link to Cycle Through Multiple Actions")

> Runs the next child action each time this action fires, wrapping back to the first child after the last. To cycle variable values, use child actions that set the variable. The runtime reads the ordered child actions, not a `values` or `variables` JSON object in BTTGenericActionConfig.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 335
*   **BTTAdditionalActions**: Ordered child actions to cycle through
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object (optional)
    *   `BTTActionCycleThroughMultipleResetAfterTimeout`: boolean - Reset to the first child after inactivity
    *   `BTTActionCycleThroughMultipleResetTimeout`: number - Inactivity timeout in seconds

Example (alternate left and right click):

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 335,  "BTTAdditionalActions": [    {"BTTPredefinedActionType": 3},    {"BTTPredefinedActionType": 4}  ]}

### Send MIDI Command[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#send-midi-command "Direct link to Send MIDI Command")

> Sends a MIDI command to a connected MIDI device / endpoint.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 462
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with the MIDI command configuration

BTTAdditionalActionData properties:

*   **BTTMidiCommandType**: Command type: `159` (Note On), `143` (Note Off), `175` (Polyphonic Key Pressure), `191` (Control Change), `207` (Program Change), `239` (Pitch Wheel Change)
*   **BTTMidiCommandNote**: Note number (0-127, Note On / Note Off / Polyphonic Key Pressure)
*   **BTTMidiCommandControllerNumber**: Controller number (0-127, Control Change only)
*   **BTTMidiCommandProgramNumber**: Program number (0-127, Program Change only)
*   **BTTMidiCommandValue**: Controller value (0-127, Control Change only)
*   **BTTMidiCommandPitchChange**: Pitch wheel value (0-16383, 8192 = centered, Pitch Wheel Change only). Pitch wheel actions saved before this field existed keep working; their 7-bit BTTMidiCommandValue is interpreted as the most significant byte.
*   **BTTMidiCommandVelocity**: Velocity (0-127, Note On / Note Off)
*   **BTTMidiCommandPressure**: Pressure (0-127, Polyphonic Key Pressure only)
*   **BTTMidiCommandChannel**: MIDI channel (0-15)
*   **BTTMidiCommandEndpoint**: Identifier of the MIDI endpoint to send to

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 462,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTMidiCommandType": 239,    "BTTMidiCommandPitchChange": 8192,    "BTTMidiCommandChannel": 0,    "BTTMidiCommandEndpoint": "IAC Driver Bus 1"  }}

### Send OSC Message[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#send-osc-message "Direct link to Send OSC Message")

> Sends an Open Sound Control (OSC) message to a UDP host/port. Arguments are provided as a JSON array.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 602
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with the OSC message configuration

BTTAdditionalActionData properties:

*   **BTTActionOSCHost**: Destination host (default `127.0.0.1`)
*   **BTTActionOSCPort**: Destination UDP port (default `8000`, range 1-65535)
*   **BTTActionOSCAddress**: OSC address pattern (default `/btt/test`)
*   **BTTActionOSCArgumentsJSON**: JSON array of arguments. Values can be plain strings/numbers/booleans or typed objects like `{"type":"f","value":0.75}`, `{"type":"i","value":1}`, `{"type":"s","value":"go"}`. BTT variables can be used in all fields.

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 602,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionOSCHost": "127.0.0.1",    "BTTActionOSCPort": 8000,    "BTTActionOSCAddress": "/btt/fader1",    "BTTActionOSCArgumentsJSON": "[{\"type\":\"f\",\"value\":0.75}]"  }}

### Send Raw Data to Generic Device[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#send-raw-data-to-generic-device "Direct link to Send Raw Data to Generic Device")

> Sends raw HID data to a device set up via BTT's Generic Devices support. Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 379
*   **BTTAdditionalActionData**: JSON object with configuration
    *   `BTTActionSendDataTargetDevice`: string - UUID of the Generic Device trigger describing the target device
    *   `BTTActionSendDataData`: string - The data to send, as a hex string (e.g. "B0B1B2")
    *   `BTTActionSendDataReportType`: number - IOHIDReportType used for sending
    *   `BTTActionSendDataResponseType`: number - IOHIDReportType expected for the response (-1 = no response expected)
    *   `BTTActionSendDataResponsePrefix`: string - Expected hex prefix of the response
    *   `BTTActionSendDataMaxPayloadSize`: number - Maximum payload size in bytes Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 379,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionSendDataTargetDevice": "UUID-OF-GENERIC-DEVICE-TRIGGER",    "BTTActionSendDataData": "B0B1B2",    "BTTActionSendDataMaxPayloadSize": 64  }}

### Find Position of Image on Screen[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#find-position-of-image-on-screen "Direct link to Find Position of Image on Screen")

> Takes a screenshot of the selected area, searches it for a reference image (template matching) and optionally moves/drags the mouse to the match, saves its position to variables and runs named triggers depending on whether it was found.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**: 291
*   **BTTFindPositionOfImageImage**: string - base64 encoded PNG of the image to search for (this is the only way to supply the image; there is no file-path option)
*   **BTTFindPositionOfImageImageDark**: string - base64 encoded PNG used instead while macOS dark mode is active. Only used when `BTTFindImageUseDifferentDarkModeImage` is true
*   **BTTFindPositionOfImageConfig**: the search configuration, as a JSON object or JSON string. It holds the following keys:
    *   `BTTFindImageUseDifferentDarkModeImage`: boolean - if true and dark mode is active, `BTTFindPositionOfImageImageDark` is used
    *   `BTTFindImageUseColor`: boolean - include color in matching; if false, matching is done on grayscale
    *   `BTTFindImageTreshold`: number 0.0 - 1.0 (note the spelling - this is the real key) - required match certainty. Higher = stricter
    *   `BTTFindImageSearchOn`: number - which area is captured and searched: 0 = all screens, 1 = screen with mouse cursor, 2 = main screen, 3 = screens without the mouse cursor, 4 = screen containing the focused window, 5 = only the focused window's rect, 6 = square area around the mouse cursor (size from `BTTFindImageSquareSize`)
    *   `BTTFindImageSquareSize`: number - edge length in points of the square centered on the mouse cursor (only for `BTTFindImageSearchOn: 6`)
    *   `BTTFindImageSearchRegion`: number - further restricts the captured area: 0 = whole area, 1-4 = top left / top right / bottom left / bottom right quarter, 5 = top half, 6 = bottom half, 7 = left half, 8 = right half
    *   `BTTFindImageSearchDirection`: number - order in which matches are collected: 0 = top left to bottom right, 1 = top right to bottom left, 2 = bottom left to top right, 3 = bottom right to top left
    *   `BTTFindImageSkipFirstMatches`: number or string - skip this many matches and use the next one (a string may contain BTT variables)
    *   `BTTFindImageMoveMouseTo`: number - where to move the mouse when found: 0 = do not move, 1 = top left of the match, 2 = center, 3 = top right, 4 = bottom left, 5 = bottom right
    *   `BTTFindImageBTTMouseMoveDuration`: number - mouse move animation duration in seconds (0 - 3)
    *   `BTTFindImageBTTMouseMoveDragType`: boolean - if set, the mouse is dragged (button held) instead of just moved
    *   `BTTFindImageSaveToVariable`: boolean - save the found location to BTT variables (see below)
    *   `BTTFindImageIfFoundTrigger`: string - name of a named trigger to run when the image was found
    *   `BTTFindImageIfNotFoundTrigger`: string - name of a named trigger to run when the image was not found
    *   `BTTFindImageContinueActionExecution`: boolean - if true, the remaining actions still run when the image was not found

When `BTTFindImageSaveToVariable` is enabled, the following BTT variables are set:

*   `image_location`: the point as a string, e.g. `{100, 200}`
*   `image_location_x`, `image_location_y`: the coordinates as numbers
*   `image_location_found`: `1` when found, `0` when not found

Note: do **not** put this configuration into `BTTAdditionalActionData` for this action - for action 291 that would overwrite the stored image data.

Example:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 291,  "BTTFindPositionOfImageImage": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUg...",  "BTTFindPositionOfImageConfig": {    "BTTFindImageUseColor": true,    "BTTFindImageTreshold": 0.85,    "BTTFindImageSearchOn": 1,    "BTTFindImageSearchRegion": 0,    "BTTFindImageSearchDirection": 0,    "BTTFindImageMoveMouseTo": 2,    "BTTFindImageBTTMouseMoveDuration": 0.2,    "BTTFindImageSaveToVariable": true,    "BTTFindImageIfNotFoundTrigger": "Image Missing Handler"  }}

### Start/Stop Scroll Blocking[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions/#startstop-scroll-blocking "Direct link to Start/Stop Scroll Blocking")

> Blocks scroll events from reaching apps.

Parameters:

*   **BTTPredefinedActionType**:
