# BTT As MCP Provider | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/external-mcp-provider/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

BetterTouchTool can expose its configured AI assistants to external MCP clients such as Codex or Claude Code.

This is controlled by the setting **Enable BetterTouchTool MCP Server For External AI Clients** (`BTTExternalMCPServerEnabled`) in BTT's MCP settings. The server listens on localhost only.

Endpoint[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/external-mcp-provider/#endpoint "Direct link to Endpoint")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The HTTP MCP endpoint is:

    http://127.0.0.1:64832/mcp

Port `64832` is the default. You can change it with `BTTExternalMCPServerPort`. For OpenCode remote MCP, BTT also provides:

    http://127.0.0.1:64832/sse

Recommended Session Flow[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/external-mcp-provider/#recommended-session-flow "Direct link to Recommended Session Flow")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

External clients should use assistant-session mode:

1.  Call `list_btt_assistants`.
2.  Pick the assistant you want to use.
3.  Call `activate_btt_assistant`.
4.  Call `load_bettertouchtool_assistant_instructions`.
5.  Follow the returned instructions for the rest of the session.

After activation, the visible tools are filtered to the selected assistant's skills and permissions. Direct MCP tools can be called directly. Other allowed BTT helper functions can be called through `run_javascript` using the `ai` object.

Codex Setup[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/external-mcp-provider/#codex-setup "Direct link to Codex Setup")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    codex mcp add btt --url http://127.0.0.1:64832/mcp

A useful first prompt in a new Codex chat:

    Use the BetterTouchTool MCP server in assistant-session mode. First call list_btt_assistants, then activate the BTT assistant I name, then call load_bettertouchtool_assistant_instructions and follow those instructions.

BTT can also install a BetterTouchTool-managed Codex plugin that uses the currently configured port.

Claude Code Setup[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/external-mcp-provider/#claude-code-setup "Direct link to Claude Code Setup")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    claude mcp add --transport http btt http://127.0.0.1:64832/mcp

Use `--scope user` to make it available across projects, or `--scope project` to write a project `.mcp.json`.

Security Notes[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/external-mcp-provider/#security-notes "Direct link to Security Notes")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This is a local bridge, not a sandbox. Any local process that can reach the configured localhost port can ask BTT's MCP server for tools. Only enable it on Macs and user accounts you trust, and keep assistant skills scoped to what external clients should be allowed to do.

*   [Endpoint](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/external-mcp-provider/#endpoint)
    
*   [Recommended Session Flow](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/external-mcp-provider/#recommended-session-flow)
    
*   [Codex Setup](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/external-mcp-provider/#codex-setup)
    
*   [Claude Code Setup](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/external-mcp-provider/#claude-code-setup)
    
*   [Security Notes](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/external-mcp-provider/#security-notes)

# Embedding Floating Menus | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/embedding-floating-menus/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

An AI Assistant can embed a BetterTouchTool floating menu inside the chat. This is helpful when the assistant is used for repeated workflows that benefit from fixed buttons, toggles, or status widgets.

![Embedded floating menu](https://docs.folivora.ai/assets/images/embedding-floating-menus2026-04-30T09:25:50.639Z-424e03975f8990e3b41423b9e86837ee.png)

Recommended setup for the embedded menu:

*   Set availability to **Only Embedded**.
*   Give the menu an explicit size, or use fit-to-content if the layout is simple.
*   Keep controls compact and task-focused.

![Floating menu setup](https://docs.folivora.ai/assets/images/embedding-floating-menus2026-04-30T09:26:38.652Z-c02bfa3bc9b8fe8cbf54d0116860fa6b.png)

# Getting Started | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/getting-started/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

1.  Add the predefined action **[h@llo.ai](mailto:h@llo.ai)
     - Show Customizable AI Assistant** to any BetterTouchTool trigger.
2.  Choose an AI backend in the assistant configuration and add the required API key, login, local server URL, or CLI setup.
3.  Open **AI Configuration -> Tools & Context -> Manage Skills...**.
4.  Enable the skills that match the assistant's job.
5.  Trigger the assistant and start with a small request.

Good First Setup[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/getting-started/#good-first-setup "Direct link to Good First Setup")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For a general BTT helper, enable:

*   **General Assistant**
*   **BTT Expert**

Then ask something simple, for example:

    Create a keyboard shortcut that shows a HUD saying "Hello".

Once that works, add more focused skills such as **Computer Use**, **Background Computer Use**, **Research Assistant**, or **Floating Menu & Widget Creator**.

Keep It Focused[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/getting-started/#keep-it-focused "Direct link to Keep It Focused")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Create separate assistants for separate jobs. A small assistant with two relevant skills is usually faster, safer, and more reliable than one assistant with every possible capability.

*   [Good First Setup](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/getting-started/#good-first-setup)
    
*   [Keep It Focused](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/getting-started/#keep-it-focused)

# Usage Without UI | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/usage-without-ui/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

AI Assistants can run without showing the chat window. This is useful for shortcuts, scheduled reports, text transformations, and background automations.

Invisible Assistant[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/usage-without-ui/#invisible-assistant "Direct link to Invisible Assistant")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In the assistant action, provide an initial user message and enable:

*   **Stop & Close After Processing Initial User Message**
*   **Invisible Operation / Don't Show UI**

This uses the same assistant configuration, skills, context, and model as the visible chat.

Run AI Task In Background[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/usage-without-ui/#run-ai-task-in-background "Direct link to Run AI Task In Background")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The predefined action **[h@llo.ai](mailto:h@llo.ai)
 - Run AI Task In Background** runs a prompt silently from any BTT trigger.

It can:

*   use a selected AI assistant
*   send a fixed or variable-based user message
*   attach a screenshot or file
*   reuse an existing conversation
*   temporarily disable selected skills
*   write the result to `BTTLastAIResult`

Use `BTTLastAIResult` in later actions to show a HUD, paste text, run a script, or update a variable.

Scheduled AI Trigger[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/usage-without-ui/#scheduled-ai-trigger "Direct link to Scheduled AI Trigger")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The **Scheduled AI Trigger** runs an AI task on an interval or CRON-like schedule.

Use it for:

*   daily briefings
*   periodic status checks
*   recurring summaries
*   automated reports

External Clients[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/usage-without-ui/#external-clients "Direct link to External Clients")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For headless control from tools such as Codex or Claude Code, enable [BTT as MCP Provider](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/external-mcp-provider)
.

*   [Invisible Assistant](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/usage-without-ui/#invisible-assistant)
    
*   [Run AI Task In Background](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/usage-without-ui/#run-ai-task-in-background)
    
*   [Scheduled AI Trigger](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/usage-without-ui/#scheduled-ai-trigger)
    
*   [External Clients](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/usage-without-ui/#external-clients)

# Subagents | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/subagents/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Subagents are specialized assistants that a main assistant can call for focused work.

Use them when a task benefits from a separate role, for example:

*   code review
*   UI testing
*   workflow building
*   research
*   plugin repair

How They Differ From Skills[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/subagents/#how-they-differ-from-skills "Direct link to How They Differ From Skills")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Skills define what the main assistant can do. Subagents are helper assistants with their own instructions, tool access, iteration limits, and optional model settings.

Some built-in skills already include useful subagents. You can also configure custom subagents and allow them from the main assistant configuration.

Good Practice[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/subagents/#good-practice "Direct link to Good Practice")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   Keep each subagent narrow.
*   Give it only the tools it needs.
*   Use a different model only when that role needs it.
*   Let the main assistant summarize the result for you.

Subagent activity is shown in the parent conversation so you can see what was delegated.

*   [How They Differ From Skills](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/subagents/#how-they-differ-from-skills)
    
*   [Good Practice](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/subagents/#good-practice)

---

# Initial Screenshot Or Message | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/initial-screenshot/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

An assistant action can start with a predefined user message, a screenshot, or both. This is useful when a trigger should immediately ask the assistant to process something without waiting for manual input.

Examples:

*   capture a selected screen region and ask the assistant to describe it
*   send the current clipboard text for summarization
*   run a fixed prompt whenever a Stream Deck button is pressed
*   attach a screenshot before a computer-use task starts

For repeated background tasks, also see [Usage Without UI](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/usage-without-ui)
.

# Persistent Memory | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/memory/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Persistent memory lets an assistant remember useful information across conversations. Memories are stored locally on your Mac and can be searched later by the assistant when memory tools are enabled.

What To Save[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/memory/#what-to-save "Direct link to What To Save")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Good memories are stable and useful:

*   preferences
*   recurring goals
*   decisions
*   facts about your setup
*   important project notes
*   todos you want the assistant to remember

Avoid saving temporary observations, passwords, API keys, or private information that should not be sent back to an AI provider in future conversations.

How It Works[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/memory/#how-it-works "Direct link to How It Works")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When a skill grants memory access, the assistant can:

*   save a memory
*   recall relevant memories
*   forget old or wrong memories

BTT can also add a compact memory bulletin to the assistant's context so it starts with the most relevant remembered information.

Storage[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/memory/#storage "Direct link to Storage")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Memories are stored in a local SQLite database:

    ~/Library/Application Support/BetterTouchTool/AI/Memory/memory.db

Even though the database is local, recalled memories become part of the assistant request and may be sent to the selected AI provider.

*   [What To Save](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/memory/#what-to-save)
    
*   [How It Works](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/memory/#how-it-works)
    
*   [Storage](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/memory/#storage)

---

# Context | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/context/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Context is information BTT adds so the assistant understands what is happening on your Mac. Skills usually choose the right context automatically.

Common Context Items[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/context/#common-context-items "Direct link to Common Context Items")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   **Date and time:** Useful for scheduling and relative dates.
*   **Selected text:** Lets the assistant explain, transform, or replace the current selection.
*   **Active application:** Helps the assistant adapt to the app you are using.
*   **Active windows:** Gives app names, window titles, bounds, and identifiers.
*   **Active document / project:** Useful for coding and document workflows.
*   **Screen information:** Lists connected displays and their coordinate spaces.
*   **Accessibility tree:** Describes controls in the frontmost app. Powerful, but can be large.
*   **Memory bulletin:** Adds relevant saved memories to the conversation.
*   **JavaScript / MCP tool definitions:** Documents the tools the assistant can call via scripting, including tools from configured [external MCP servers](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/mcp)
    .

Keep It Small[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/context/#keep-it-small "Direct link to Keep It Small")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

More context can make an assistant smarter, but it also makes requests slower and more expensive. Avoid enabling screenshots, accessibility trees, or large project context unless the assistant's skill needs them.

Custom Context[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/context/#custom-context "Direct link to Custom Context")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

You can create dynamic custom context from **Automations, Named & Other Triggers** using **[h@llo.ai](mailto:h@llo.ai)
 - Custom AI Context**.

Custom context can call BTT JavaScript, read variables, inspect app state, or provide any small text summary the assistant should see.

*   [Common Context Items](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/context/#common-context-items)
    
*   [Keep It Small](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/context/#keep-it-small)
    
*   [Custom Context](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/context/#custom-context)

---

# Skills | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/skills/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Skills are the main way to configure AI Assistants in BetterTouchTool. Instead of manually picking many individual tools, choose skills that describe what the assistant should be able to do.

A skill can provide:

*   system instructions
*   allowed tools
*   context items
*   subagents
*   thinking settings
*   example prompts
*   file access limits

Active, Optional, Or Off[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/skills/#active-optional-or-off "Direct link to Active, Optional, Or Off")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In **AI Configuration -> Tools & Context -> Manage Skills...**, each skill can be set to:

*   **Active:** Loaded whenever the assistant starts.
*   **Optional:** Available on demand. The assistant can request it when the task needs it.
*   **Off:** Not available to that assistant.

Use **Active** for the assistant's normal job. Use **Optional** for powerful or occasional capabilities such as plugin creation, shell access, or background computer use.

Built-In Skills[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/skills/#built-in-skills "Direct link to Built-In Skills")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   **General Assistant:** Writing, questions, selected text, web lookup, and everyday help.
*   **BTT Expert:** BetterTouchTool documentation, triggers, actions, snippets, and configuration changes.
*   **Computer Use:** Frontmost visible app control with screenshots, accessibility, keyboard, mouse, windows, and menu bar tools.
*   **Background Computer Use:** Targeted background window control without activating the app.
*   **Desktop Automation:** General macOS automation using BTT's desktop tools.
*   **Floating Menu & Widget Creator:** Floating menus and Swift widget plugins.
*   **BTT Plugin Creator / Editor:** JSON action plugins and native Swift plugins.
*   **Code Assistant:** File editing, shell commands, diagnostics, and project work.
*   **Research Assistant:** Web research, document reading, and memory.
*   **Safari Automation:** Browser automation and page inspection.

MCP Server Skills[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/skills/#mcp-server-skills "Direct link to MCP Server Skills")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every external MCP server configured in BTT automatically becomes its own skill in the **MCP Servers** category, granting all tools that server provides. These skills are offered to assistants as optional skills by default and can be edited like any other skill — see [External MCP Servers](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/mcp)
 for details.

Custom Skills[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/skills/#custom-skills "Direct link to Custom Skills")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

You can create, duplicate, edit, and import skills from the skill manager. Custom BTT skills are stored here:

    ~/Library/Application Support/BetterTouchTool/AI/Skills/custom

BTT can also load OpenClaw-style `SKILL.md` folders from:

    ~/Library/Application Support/BetterTouchTool/AI/Skills/openclaw~/.openclaw/skills

Practical Tips[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/skills/#practical-tips "Direct link to Practical Tips")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   Prefer one or two focused skills over a large collection of unrelated skills.
*   Keep risky skills optional unless they are central to the assistant.
*   Create task-specific assistants rather than one assistant with every capability.
*   If a background or computer-use workflow behaves oddly, use the matching dedicated skill instead of generic automation tools.

*   [Active, Optional, Or Off](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/skills/#active-optional-or-off)
    
*   [Built-In Skills](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/skills/#built-in-skills)
    
*   [MCP Server Skills](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/skills/#mcp-server-skills)
    
*   [Custom Skills](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/skills/#custom-skills)
    
*   [Practical Tips](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/skills/#practical-tips)

# API Keys And Models | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/api-keys/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

BetterTouchTool AI Assistants work with multiple model backends. You can use cloud APIs, compatible local servers, or command line tools.

Supported Backends[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/api-keys/#supported-backends "Direct link to Supported Backends")

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   **OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible APIs**
*   **OpenAI Responses-compatible APIs**
*   **Anthropic / compatible APIs**
*   **ChatGPT Codex subscription**
*   **Claude Code CLI**
*   **Codex CLI**
*   **OpenCode CLI**
*   **Apple Foundation Models** on supported macOS versions
*   **Local OpenAI-compatible servers**, such as LM Studio or Ollama
*   **Aggregator services**, such as OpenRouter or other compatible providers

Setup[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/api-keys/#setup "Direct link to Setup")

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Create an API key or sign in using the provider's normal setup flow.
2.  In the assistant configuration, choose the matching API type.
3.  Paste the key or configure the local command/server URL.
4.  Pick a model that supports the features you want to use.
5.  Set a spending limit with the provider when using paid cloud APIs.

For local OpenAI-compatible servers, common URLs are:

    LM Studio: http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/chat/completionsOllama:    http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions

Choosing A Model[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/api-keys/#choosing-a-model "Direct link to Choosing A Model")

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Use a strong cloud model for automation, BTT configuration changes, plugin creation, and computer use. Smaller or local models are often fine for summarizing text, rewriting selected text, and simple chat.

Tool use quality matters more than raw chat quality for automation assistants. If an assistant seems to ignore tools, choose a model with better tool-calling support or reduce the number of active skills.

Privacy[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/api-keys/#privacy "Direct link to Privacy")

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

BTT sends assistant messages, enabled context, tool results, and attachments directly to the selected provider. Keep sensitive context and powerful skills disabled unless they are needed for the current assistant.

*   [Supported Backends](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/api-keys/#supported-backends)
    
*   [Setup](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/api-keys/#setup)
    
*   [Choosing A Model](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/api-keys/#choosing-a-model)
    
*   [Privacy](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/api-keys/#privacy)

On this page

The best assistants are now usually skill combinations, not long manual tool lists.

Useful Starting Points[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/example-assistants/#useful-starting-points "Direct link to Useful Starting Points")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   **BTT helper:** General Assistant + BTT Expert
*   **Visible app operator:** General Assistant + Computer Use

*   **Research helper:** Research Assistant + Memory

*   **Plugin builder:** BTT Expert + BTT Plugin Creator as an optional skill

Importable Example[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/example-assistants/#importable-example "Direct link to Importable Example")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Review its enabled skills and permissions before using it. Automation assistants can click, type, run scripts, and change BTT configuration.

# Tools | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/tools/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Tools are the low-level actions an assistant can call. Skills decide which tools are available, so most users should configure [Skills](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/skills)
 first and only adjust individual tools for advanced use cases.

Common Tool Groups[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/tools/#common-tool-groups "Direct link to Common Tool Groups")

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   **BTT configuration:** Search native action and trigger names/IDs and configuration references, look up covered native schema fields, validate JSON before writes, create or update triggers, edit action lists, create snippets, and inspect exported results. The updated creation tool requires matching native names for new top-level trackpad and Magic Mouse gestures. See the [JSON configuration workflow](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/json/overview)
    .
*   **Plugin authoring:** Retrieve the reference for a Swift or JSON plugin type, edit source, compile Swift plugins, and validate embedded action JSON. See [Creating Plugins With AI](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring)
    .
*   **Computer use:** Screenshots, windows, accessibility trees, UI element search, clicks, typing, shortcuts, OCR, and menu bar actions.
*   **Background computer use:** Targeted background clicks, shortcuts, key presses, scrolling, window state, app launching, and fake cursor display.
*   **Text workflows:** Read selected text, transform it, replace it, paste text, and update the clipboard.
*   **Files and code:** Read, write, search, edit, diff, patch, run diagnostics, and execute scripts when the skill allows it.
*   **Web and research:** Search the web, fetch pages, inspect browser content, and automate Safari.
*   **Memory:** Save, recall, and forget persistent memories.
*   **UI output:** Show HUDs, status messages, interactive chat content, and files.
*   **MCP:** Use tools from configured external MCP servers. Each server automatically becomes its own skill — see [External MCP Servers](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/mcp)
    .

When To Edit Tools Manually[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/tools/#when-to-edit-tools-manually "Direct link to When To Edit Tools Manually")

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Manual tool selection is useful when you want a very narrow assistant, when you are migrating an older setup, or when a custom skill needs one extra capability.

For new assistants, prefer this order:

1.  Pick the right built-in skill.
2.  Add a custom skill if the workflow is recurring.
3.  Only then add or remove individual tools.

Custom User Tools[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/tools/#custom-user-tools "Direct link to Custom User Tools")

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Custom tools can be created from BetterTouchTool Named Triggers. This is useful when you already have a trusted BTT automation and want an assistant to call it by name.

Safety[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/tools/#safety "Direct link to Safety")

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Tools such as shell scripts, AppleScript, file writes, plugin compilation, and desktop control can affect your Mac directly. Keep powerful tools inside focused skills and avoid granting full access to general chat assistants.

*   [Common Tool Groups](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/tools/#common-tool-groups)
    
*   [When To Edit Tools Manually](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/tools/#when-to-edit-tools-manually)
    
*   [Custom User Tools](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/tools/#custom-user-tools)
    
*   [Safety](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/tools/#safety)

# Extended Thinking | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/extended-thinking/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Some models support extra reasoning or thinking controls. BTT can enable these globally on an assistant or through a skill.

Use extended thinking for:

*   BTT configuration changes with many details
*   computer-use tasks that need planning and verification
*   plugin creation
*   code changes
*   longer research or analysis

Leave it off for quick rewriting, short answers, and simple one-step automations.

Levels[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/extended-thinking/#levels "Direct link to Levels")

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

BTT offers levels from **Minimal** to **Maximum**, plus **Adaptive** where supported. Higher levels can improve difficult tasks, but they also increase latency and provider cost.

Newer Claude models only support adaptive thinking, where the model decides when and how much to think. For these models BTT automatically switches to adaptive mode and translates the selected level into a matching effort setting.

When multiple active skills request thinking, BTT uses the strongest requested setting. If any skill requests adaptive, adaptive wins.

Provider Support[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/extended-thinking/#provider-support "Direct link to Provider Support")

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Provider support varies. Some cloud models expose explicit thinking budgets, some expose reasoning effort, and some local models ignore these settings. If a model does not support extended thinking, BTT continues with the normal request.

*   [Levels](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/extended-thinking/#levels)
    
*   [Provider Support](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/ai-assistants/extended-thinking/#provider-support)

# Notch Bar (Deprecated) | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/notch-bar/overview/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

### Deprecation Notice 06/2023:[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/notch-bar/overview/#deprecation-notice-062023 "Direct link to Deprecation Notice 06/2023:")

The Notch Bar functionality will sometime in the near future be migrated to the powerful new "Floating Menu / Widget" functionality. This should mostly be automatic, but if you start right now, I'd recommend to experiment with the Floating Menus instead of the Notch Bar.

* * *

The Notch Bar was introduced with BetterTouchTool 3.690 and is intended to be a super customizable menubar replacement for any type of Mac. It is called Notch Bar, because it is especially useful on MacBooks with a Notch. ![notchbar](https://docs.folivora.ai/assets/images/notchbar-5f7aaf3a6f28ded0a9d72a6bf9af9ac4.jpg)

Also have a look at this recent MacStories article: [MacStories: Early Experiments with BetterTouchTool's Notch Bar](https://www.macstories.net/mac/early-experiments-with-bettertouchtools-notch-bar-as-a-visual-shortcuts-launcher-for-macos/)

Example Preset[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/notch-bar/overview/#example-preset "Direct link to Example Preset")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Here is a small example preset that showcases most of the Notch Bar functionality:

[Example Preset Direct Link](https://folivora.ai/releases/ExampleNotchBarNew.bttpreset)

Quick Start[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/notch-bar/overview/#quick-start "Direct link to Quick Start")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   If possible, **please use a dark wallpaper**, so your standard macOS menubar shows white icons and white text. In this mode the BTT Notch Bar works best.
    
*   As soon as you add your first Notch Bar trigger, your macOS menubar will go away. To hide the BTT Notch Bar use the predefined action "Toggle BTT Notch Bar" or right-click the black area.
    
*   The BTT Notch Bar offers two modes: **Widget Mode** and **Menubar Mode**. To switch between modes, **scroll up/down on the Notch Bar**, alternatively use the predefined action "Toggle BTT Notch Bar Mode" or right-click the Notch Bar.
    
*   Use the **Status Item Widget** to show the system's top right status items on the BTT Notch Bar.
    
*   There is currently a known incompatibility with an app called Magnet. The Notch Bar does not behave correctly while this app is running.
    

**Please use the community platform to learn more or share your ideas / setups**:

[https://community.folivora.ai](https://community.folivora.ai/)

More Notch Bar Topics:
======================

# JSON Definitions | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/json/overview/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Triggers, actions and floating menus can be exported as JSON and imported again. Copy a configured trigger or action in BTT and paste it into a text editor to see its exported properties.

The references below cover many legacy settings, but coverage is partial. Use definitions from the running BTT when configuring it with AI, because accepted keys, value encodings and supported options can differ between versions.

*   [All Predefined Actions JSON Definitions](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/actions/action-definitions)
    
*   [All Trigger JSON Definitions](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/json/trigger-definitions)
    
*   [Floating Menu JSON Definitions](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/json/floating-menu)
    

AI Configuration Workflow[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/json/overview/#ai-configuration-workflow "Direct link to AI Configuration Workflow")

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Read the target's current JSON when editing existing configuration. Identify its UUID, application, preset and action category.
2.  Use `lookup_btt_action_definition` with an `action_id` for the full action section and native schema. Confirm fixed gesture IDs with `lookup_btt_trigger_definition(trigger_id: ...)`, then read the matching category or floating-menu reference. The running app's native names and IDs take precedence over prose and web search. Finger count, swipe direction and device class must all match.
3.  Construct JSON using the documented key locations and value representations. A form control's internal ID is not necessarily its exported JSON key.
4.  Run `validate_btt_trigger_json`. When validating a patch, pass `existing_trigger_uuid` and the same `replace_action_data` setting planned for the update. For floating menus, also run `validate_floating_menu_json`. Fix errors and review warnings before writing.
5.  Use the appropriate create or update tool, following the native-name requirements below for trackpad and Magic Mouse gestures. Inspect exported readback and returned UUIDs. Confirm the app scope, preset, enabled state, values and child order. Compare `BTTTriggerTypeDescriptionReadOnly` and every `BTTPredefinedActionName` with the requested behavior. A custom `BTTTriggerTypeDescription` only changes a label. Repair mismatches and read the result again before reporting success.

Native schemas describe covered fields, choices and known defaults. Choices are exhaustive only when `optionsComplete` is true. An editor default can differ from the value used at runtime when a key is omitted. A preserved key outside partial schema coverage is not proof that the action consumes it.

Validation checks structure and covered fields. An import/export round trip checks persistence. Verify that the trigger fires and the action behaves as intended separately.

Creating Trackpad and Magic Mouse Gestures[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/json/overview/#creating-trackpad-and-magic-mouse-gestures "Direct link to Creating Trackpad and Magic Mouse Gestures")

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In the updated AI tools, `create_new_btt_trigger_from_json` requires the intended gesture's exact native name when creating a top-level trackpad or Magic Mouse gesture. Look up the gesture first and supply the name in one of these places:

*   **Single trigger:** pass `expected_trigger_name` as a tool argument alongside `trigger_json`. It is not a property inside the trigger JSON.
*   **JSON or batch creation:** include `BTTTriggerTypeDescriptionReadOnly` in each top-level trackpad or Magic Mouse trigger object. For a batch, use this per-object field instead of the single-trigger tool argument.

The tool compares the supplied name with the native name of `BTTTriggerType`, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace. Missing required names or mismatches stop the call before import begins. These checks also run inside the creation tool even if a separate structural validation passed. Preserve the intended gesture name and correct the ID after a mismatch; changing the name to fit a wrong ID would still create the wrong gesture.

This requirement applies to the AI creation tool. Ordinary JSON/preset imports treat `BTTTriggerTypeDescriptionReadOnly` as display metadata. Keyboard shortcut descriptions and triggers created under a parent do not have this mandatory name check.

Updating Existing Configuration[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/json/overview/#updating-existing-configuration "Direct link to Updating Existing Configuration")

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

`update_btt_trigger` requires an existing target. In the updated AI tools, `BTTAdditionalActionData` merges by key unless `replace_action_data: true` is supplied or a different action type is supplied with new action data. The tool rejects child/action arrays; use `manage_trigger_actions` to change action lists. Other containers retain their replacement behavior, so inspect their current values before replacing them.

Inspect the installed tool's parameter descriptions when working with older BTT builds. If a write reports a partial failure, read the current configuration before retrying to avoid duplicates. The legacy importer does not make every batch atomic.

Plugin source files and `.bttjsonplugin` files have their own installation workflow. See [Creating Plugins With AI](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring)
; trigger creation does not install plugin source code.

*   [AI Configuration Workflow](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/json/overview/#ai-configuration-workflow)
    
*   [Creating Trackpad and Magic Mouse Gestures](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/json/overview/#creating-trackpad-and-magic-mouse-gestures)
    
*   [Updating Existing Configuration](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/json/overview/#updating-existing-configuration)

# JSON Action Plugins | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

JSON Action Plugins are a simple way to create reusable, configurable action plugins for BetterTouchTool - **without writing any compiled code**. Instead of building an Xcode project, you write a single `.bttjsonplugin` file containing:

*   **Metadata** - plugin name, identifier, description, and icon
*   **Form fields** - user-configurable parameters that appear in the BTT preferences
*   **Actions** - a sequence of BTT actions (same format as exported presets) with placeholders that get replaced by the form field values at execution time

Quick Start[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#quick-start "Direct link to Quick Start")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Create a file with the `.bttjsonplugin` extension (e.g. `MyPlugin.bttjsonplugin`). The easiest way to do that is to right-click one or multiple actions you have configured in BTT and choose "Export Selected Actions As JSON Action Plugin".
2.  Drop it into either `~/Library/Application Support/BetterTouchTool/Plugins/` or `/Library/Application Support/BetterTouchTool/Plugins/` (or drag it onto the BTT window)
3.  In BTT, create a trigger and select your plugin from **Custom Plugin Actions**

File Format[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#file-format "Direct link to File Format")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A `.bttjsonplugin` file is a JSON file with three top-level sections:

    {  "BTTPluginMetadata": {    "BTTPluginName": "Example",    "BTTPluginIdentifier": "com.example.plugin"  },  "BTTPluginFormFields": [],  "BTTPluginActions": []}

### BTTPluginMetadata[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#bttpluginmetadata "Direct link to BTTPluginMetadata")

Describes the plugin in the action selector and plugin manager.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BTTPluginName` | String | Yes | Display name shown in the action selector |
| `BTTPluginIdentifier` | String | Yes | Unique reverse-domain identifier (e.g. `com.yourname.pluginName`) |
| `BTTPluginDescription` | String | No  | Short description of what the plugin does |
| `BTTPluginIcon` | String | No  | SF Symbol name for the icon (e.g. `star.fill`). Defaults to `puzzlepiece.extension.fill` |
| `BTTPluginVersion` | String | No  | Version string (e.g. `1.0`) |

    {  "BTTPluginName": "My Custom Action",  "BTTPluginIdentifier": "com.example.myCustomAction",  "BTTPluginDescription": "Does something useful",  "BTTPluginIcon": "bolt.fill",  "BTTPluginVersion": "1.0"}

### BTTPluginFormFields[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#bttpluginformfields "Direct link to BTTPluginFormFields")

An array of form field definitions. These create the configuration UI that appears when the user selects the plugin action. Each field's value is available as a placeholder in the actions.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `formFieldType` | String | Yes | The form field type (see table below) |
| `formFieldID` | String | For value fields | Unique plain ID for this field. Used as the placeholder name: `@@@fieldID@@@` |
| `formFieldID2` | String | For two-field items | Distinct ID for the second input of `BTTFormTypeTwoTextFields` |
| `formLabel1` | String | No  | Primary label displayed next to the field |
| `formLabel2` | String | No  | Secondary label |
| `defaultValue` | Any | No  | Initial editor value; not an execution-time fallback for missing saved values |
| `dataType` | Number | No  | `1` = String, `2` = Number, `3` = JSON, `5` = Icon, `6` = Data |
| `minValue` | Number | No  | Minimum value (for sliders) |
| `maxValue` | Number | No  | Maximum value (for sliders) |
| `formOptions` | Array | No  | Options for popup buttons (see below) |

#### Available Form Field Types[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#available-form-field-types "Direct link to Available Form Field Types")

| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `BTTFormTypeTextField` | Single-line text input |
| `BTTFormTypeTwoTextFields` | Two text fields side by side, bound to `formFieldID` and `formFieldID2` |
| `BTTFormTypeTextArea` | Multi-line text input |
| `BTTFormTypeCheckbox` | Boolean toggle |
| `BTTFormTypeSlider` | Numeric slider (set `minValue`, `maxValue`, `dataType` to `2`) |
| `BTTFormTypePopupButton` | Dropdown selector. If `defaultValue` is omitted, BTT uses the first option. |
| `BTTFormTypeColorPicker` | Color picker |
| `BTTFormTypeImagePicker` | Image picker (value is Base64 encoded) |
| `BTTFormTypeSeparator` | Visual separator line (no value) |
| `BTTFormTypeDescription` | Static description text (use `formLabel1` for content) |

The JSON loader supports the fields and types listed here. It loads flat fields and popup options; it does not recursively decode the nested form groups available to Swift plugins. Use `BTTFormTypeDescription` for static text.

Use plain IDs such as `title`. Saved action configuration uses `plugin_var_title`; the placeholder remains `@@@title@@@`. Both inputs of a two-field item use the same prefix normalization.

#### Popup Button Options[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#popup-button-options "Direct link to Popup Button Options")

For `BTTFormTypePopupButton`, provide an array of option objects:

    {  "formFieldType": "BTTFormTypePopupButton",  "formFieldID": "position",  "formLabel1": "Position:",  "defaultValue": "top",  "formOptions": [    { "formLabel1": "Top", "formOption": "top" },    { "formLabel1": "Center", "formOption": "center" },    { "formLabel1": "Bottom", "formOption": "bottom" }  ]}

### BTTPluginActions[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#bttpluginactions "Direct link to BTTPluginActions")

An array of BTT action dictionaries - the same JSON format used when exporting triggers/actions from BTT. These actions are executed in sequence when the plugin is triggered.

Use `@@@fieldID@@@` placeholders inside JSON string values. BTT substitutes JSON-escaped text from the saved configuration at execution time. This example is the value of `BTTPluginActions`, assuming form fields named `hudTitle` and `duration`:

    [  {    "BTTPredefinedActionType": 254,    "BTTAdditionalActionData": {      "BTTActionHUDTitle": "@@@hudTitle@@@",      "BTTActionHUDDuration": "@@@duration@@@"    }  }]

Getting the action JSON

The easiest way to get the correct action JSON is to:

1.  Configure the action manually in BTT
2.  Right-click the trigger > **Copy JSON**
3.  Extract the action properties from the exported JSON
4.  Replace the values you want to be configurable with `@@@fieldID@@@` placeholders

Complete Example[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#complete-example "Direct link to Complete Example")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This plugin shows a configurable BTT HUD message:

    {  "BTTPluginMetadata": {    "BTTPluginName": "Show HUD Message",    "BTTPluginIdentifier": "com.example.showNotification",    "BTTPluginDescription": "Shows a BTT HUD with a custom title and message",    "BTTPluginIcon": "bell.fill",    "BTTPluginVersion": "1.0"  },  "BTTPluginFormFields": [    {      "formFieldType": "BTTFormTypeTextField",      "formFieldID": "notifTitle",      "formLabel1": "HUD Title:",      "defaultValue": "Hello",      "dataType": 1    },    {      "formFieldType": "BTTFormTypeTextField",      "formFieldID": "notifMessage",      "formLabel1": "HUD Message:",      "defaultValue": "World",      "dataType": 1    }  ],  "BTTPluginActions": [    {      "BTTPredefinedActionType": 254,      "BTTAdditionalActionData": {        "BTTActionHUDTitle": "@@@notifTitle@@@",        "BTTActionHUDDetail": "@@@notifMessage@@@",        "BTTActionHUDDuration": 2      }    }  ]}

When the user saves "HUD Title" as `Meeting Reminder` and "HUD Message" as `Standup in 5 minutes`, BTT replaces the placeholders and executes:

    {  "BTTPredefinedActionType": 254,  "BTTAdditionalActionData": {    "BTTActionHUDTitle": "Meeting Reminder",    "BTTActionHUDDetail": "Standup in 5 minutes",    "BTTActionHUDDuration": 2  }}

Placeholder Replacement[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#placeholder-replacement "Direct link to Placeholder Replacement")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   Placeholders use `@@@fieldID@@@`, matching a plain `formFieldID` or `formFieldID2`.
*   Put placeholders inside quoted JSON strings. Replacement inserts text; numbers and booleans become text too. It does not inject typed objects or arrays or evaluate expressions.
*   Values are JSON-escaped, including quotes, backslashes and newlines. Replacement operates on the serialized action JSON and also reaches strings inside nested objects.
*   A missing saved value leaves its placeholder unchanged. Form defaults initialize the editor; the executor does not independently merge defaults into unsaved configuration.
*   Keep action identities and property names literal. Use a placeholder for a numeric option only when that action accepts a numeric string; check its action definition.

Validating an AI-Generated Plugin[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#validating-an-ai-generated-plugin "Direct link to Validating an AI-Generated Plugin")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Parse the whole file as JSON and check its metadata and flat form definitions. Retrieve exact action fields with `lookup_btt_action_definition`, then validate a concrete copy of `BTTPluginActions` with `validate_btt_trigger_json`. Substitute representative values for that check, including text with quotes, backslashes and newlines.

Action validation checks the embedded actions, not the surrounding plugin metadata or form schema. Save the `.bttjsonplugin` file with a file tool; do not send it to `compile_swift_plugin`. Check that BTT loads it, that its configuration fields persist, and that executing it produces the intended result. See the [AI authoring workflow](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring)
.

Multiple Actions[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#multiple-actions "Direct link to Multiple Actions")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Include additional complete action dictionaries in the `BTTPluginActions` array. They run in sequence, like additional actions on a regular BTT trigger. Use each action's documented wait or completion settings when later actions depend on asynchronous work finishing.

Installation[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#installation "Direct link to Installation")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

JSON action plugins can be installed in several ways:

*   **File copy**: Place the `.bttjsonplugin` file in either `~/Library/Application Support/BetterTouchTool/Plugins/` or `/Library/Application Support/BetterTouchTool/Plugins/`
*   **Drag and drop**: Drag the file onto the BetterTouchTool preferences window
*   **Double-click**: Double-click the `.bttjsonplugin` file (BTT is registered as the handler)

Plugins are loaded automatically when BTT starts. If you add, modify, or remove a `.bttjsonplugin` file while BTT is running, it will detect the change and reload automatically.

Plugin Manager[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#plugin-manager "Direct link to Plugin Manager")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

JSON action plugins appear in the BTT Plugin Manager (accessible from the BTT menu bar) alongside compiled plugins. From there you can:

*   View all installed plugins
*   Reveal a plugin file in Finder
*   Delete a plugin

Comparison with Compiled Action Plugins[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#comparison-with-compiled-action-plugins "Direct link to Comparison with Compiled Action Plugins")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

| Feature | JSON Action Plugin (`.bttjsonplugin`) | Compiled Action Plugin (`.bttactionplugin`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Format** | Single JSON file | Xcode bundle |
| **Code required** | JSON; embedded actions may contain scripts | Swift or Objective-C |
| **Setup** | Text editor only | Swift source file or Xcode project |
| **Capabilities** | Existing BTT actions, including scripting and network actions | Native code with a persistent plugin object |
| **Distribution** | Share the file directly | Share Swift source, or notarize a compiled bundle |
| **Configuration UI** | Flat JSON form fields | Swift form items |
| **Use case** | Reusable action sequences, sharing action recipes | Logic that needs native APIs or a persistent object |

JSON action plugins package reusable configurations without compilation. Their actions can still run scripts and perform other operations, so inspect the action sequence when installing one. Use a Launcher or Floating Menu Widget plugin for a custom native view.

*   [Quick Start](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#quick-start)
    
*   [File Format](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#file-format)
    *   [BTTPluginMetadata](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#bttpluginmetadata)
        
    *   [BTTPluginFormFields](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#bttpluginformfields)
        
    *   [BTTPluginActions](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#bttpluginactions)
        
*   [Complete Example](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#complete-example)
    
*   [Placeholder Replacement](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#placeholder-replacement)
    
*   [Validating an AI-Generated Plugin](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#validating-an-ai-generated-plugin)
    
*   [Multiple Actions](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#multiple-actions)
    
*   [Installation](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#installation)
    
*   [Plugin Manager](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins/#plugin-manager)

# Creating Plugins With AI | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring/#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Use BTT's **Plugin Creator / Editor** skills to create or change a plugin. The assistant should retrieve the matching reference from your running BTT before generating code. That reference contains the API and examples available to that build.

Choose the Reference[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring/#choose-the-reference "Direct link to Choose the Reference")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

| Plugin | Reference tool |
| --- | --- |
| [Launcher](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/launcher) | `retrieve_launcher_plugin_reference` |
| [Action](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/action) | `retrieve_action_plugin_reference` |
| [Floating Menu Widget](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget) | `retrieve_floating_menu_widget_plugin_reference` |
| [Stream Deck](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck) | `retrieve_stream_deck_plugin_reference` |
| [Touch Bar](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/touch-bar) | `retrieve_touch_bar_plugin_reference` |
| [Trigger](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/trigger) | `retrieve_trigger_plugin_reference` |
| [JSON Action](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins) | `retrieve_json_action_plugin_reference` |

JSON action plugins package existing BTT actions and form fields. They can include scripting or network actions. Choose Swift when the plugin needs native views or a persistent object with lifecycle callbacks.

Swift Workflow[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring/#swift-workflow "Direct link to Swift Workflow")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Read the matching reference. For an existing plugin, read its current source and preserve its identifier and configuration keys.
2.  Use the exact protocol signatures from `BTTSwiftPluginHeader.h`. Keep metadata in the first 50 lines and the principal class declaration on one line. See [Swift Source Plugins](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins)
    .
3.  For a new file, call `compile_swift_plugin` with `source_code` and `plugin_file_name`. For an existing file, make focused edits, then call it with `swift_file_path`.
4.  Read compiler diagnostics and correct errors, including “nearly matches optional requirement” warnings. Those warnings can mean that BTT will never call the method.
5.  After `SUCCESS:`, configure the plugin in BTT and verify its behavior. Compilation and loading do not verify configuration persistence, keyboard handling, timers or hardware events.

The compile tool handles watcher suppression. Adding `BTT-AI-Managed` to the source does not suppress prompts in the current loader. Direct `source_code` input also avoids an extra JavaScript string-escaping layer.

For Launcher plugins, check stable result IDs, saved-instance editing, async results, keyboard commands and surface cleanup. A surface refresh updates chrome and layout; update the retained view or observable model to change its content.

JSON Workflow[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring/#json-workflow "Direct link to JSON Workflow")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Build a valid JSON object containing metadata, flat form definitions and an action array. Use a stable `BTTPluginIdentifier` and distinct field IDs.
2.  Look up each action with `lookup_btt_action_definition`. Preserve exact key locations and value encodings.
3.  Put `@@@fieldID@@@` placeholders inside JSON strings. Substitution inserts escaped text, not typed JSON or evaluated expressions.
4.  Validate a concrete copy of the action array with `validate_btt_trigger_json`, using representative form values. Check metadata and form definitions separately.
5.  Save the `.bttjsonplugin` file, select it in BTT, save its configuration and verify execution. JSON plugins do not use `compile_swift_plugin`.

See [JSON Action Plugins](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/json-action-plugins)
 for supported fields, missing-value behavior and a complete example.

Tool Availability[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring/#tool-availability "Direct link to Tool Availability")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Tools depend on the active skills and the installed BTT version. Enable the matching creator/editor skill if its reference or compilation tools are missing. Inside BTT's `run_javascript`, `ai.getAvailableTools()` lists the tool functions available to that JavaScript context. Other AI clients should use their connected BTT tool list; do not assume an unlisted helper exists.

For trigger and action configuration around the plugin, follow the [JSON configuration workflow](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/json/overview)
.

*   [Choose the Reference](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring/#choose-the-reference)
    
*   [Swift Workflow](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring/#swift-workflow)
    
*   [JSON Workflow](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring/#json-workflow)
    
*   [Tool Availability](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring/#tool-availability)
