# BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/surfaces#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Each item has a **Placement** setting in its **Macro Pad** section, which decides which part of the device it uses. The section is only shown once the enclosing menu is bound to a pad.

Placement[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/surfaces#placement "Direct link to Placement")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   **Automatic** — knob items go to the dials and are also mirrored onto the LCD strip; everything else goes to the keys.
*   **LCD Keys** — always a key.
*   **Dials / Knobs** — bound to a dial only, _not_ mirrored onto the strip. Use this when you want the strip entirely to yourself.
*   **LCD Strip** — placed on the strip, in addition to any mirrored knobs.
*   **Buttons Without Display** — placed on the pad's plain physical buttons, such as the 8 round buttons of a Loupedeck. See below.

Size and position[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/surfaces#size-and-position "Direct link to Size and position")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Items are rendered at the size you set (**Item Size**), with their **margins** included. On the LCD strip items are packed left to right: the second item starts exactly where the first ends, so sizes and margins alone decide the layout.

There is no automatic scaling — what you set is what the device shows. An item wider than its key will extend past it, which you can use deliberately for edge-to-edge artwork.

Row breakers[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/surfaces#row-breakers "Direct link to Row breakers")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A **Row Breaker** item makes the next item start on a new row of the key grid. Use it to group keys without padding the gaps with empty dummy items.

It only ever affects items that come after it, which means it quietly does nothing in the cases where you wouldn't want it to:

*   at the very end of your key items — so a breaker you added purely to separate the keys from the knob items in the on-screen menu changes nothing on the device;
*   at the very start;
*   when the next free key already begins a row;
*   directly after another breaker, so you never get a surprise blank row.

Column Breakers have no equivalent on a fixed key grid and are ignored. Row breakers are also ignored on Stream Decks driven through the Stream Deck plugin, since there is no physical grid in that mode.

Knobs[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/surfaces#knobs "Direct link to Knobs")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Add a **Knob** item and place it on the dials. Knob items have their own action categories:

*   Actions Executed On Rotate Left / Right
*   Actions Executed On Rotate Left / Right (While Pressed) — hold the knob down while turning for a second layer
*   Actions Executed On Knob Tap / Click, and on knob press down / up

A knob can show a value as a gauge (fixed range) or as an endless dial, and its gauge follows the physical knob live when it's shown on a strip.

Note that pressing and turning at the same time is treated as one gesture: the tap action does not also fire.

Buttons and knobs without a display[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/surfaces#buttons-and-knobs-without-a-display "Direct link to Buttons and knobs without a display")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Some pads have plain buttons or knobs with no screen. They work exactly like other items — they simply can't show anything.

To put an item on one, set its placement to **Buttons Without Display**. Items with that placement fill the pad's display-less buttons in the normal item order, so the order of those items decides which physical button each one gets.

On **Loupedeck and Razer Stream Controller** devices the 8 round buttons have a colour LED rather than a display, so an item placed on one lights it in that item's own colour. It's not a picture, but it is visual feedback.

On pads with only a few plain buttons (such as the AKP03 and M18), those buttons also still pick up ordinary items automatically once the keys with displays are full — the placement above simply lets you target them on purpose instead.

Side strips[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/surfaces#side-strips "Direct link to Side strips")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Some devices have narrow display strips beside the keys instead of one wide strip below them — the AKP153 has one down the side, Loupedeck devices have one on each side. Place items on them with the **LCD Strip** placement. Items fill the strips in item order, top to bottom; on Loupedeck the left strip fills before the right one.

Unlike a wide touch strip, side strips are laid out in fixed segments that line up with the key rows next to them.

Paging[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/surfaces#paging "Direct link to Paging")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If a menu has more key items than the device has keys, the last two keys that have a display become previous/next page controls, and they only appear when there is somewhere to go.

To style paging yourself, add an item and set **Macro Pad Navigation** to _Previous Page_, _Next Page_ or _Back_. Such an item is styled like any other item and replaces the default chevron. A **Back Button** item is used automatically as the back control inside submenus.

On devices with a touch strip you can also swipe left and right to change pages.

Submenus[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/surfaces#submenus "Direct link to Submenus")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A submenu item opens on the device, and a back control returns from it — the same structure you use in an on-screen menu.

# BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/setup#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

This is a very new feature

Driving a macro pad from a Floating Menu is new and still evolving. Some things are not possible yet, and details may still change between versions. Feedback is very welcome — especially if you have a device that isn't recognised.

If you want the established, fully featured configuration for Elgato Stream Decks, use the [Stream Deck section](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/stream-deck/overview)
 instead. It continues to work and is not going away; the two approaches exist side by side, and a device can only be driven by one of them at a time.

1\. Create a Floating Menu[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/setup#1-create-a-floating-menu "Direct link to 1. Create a Floating Menu")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Go to **Custom Floating Menus / Widgets** and add a Floating Menu, or start from one of the macro pad templates.

2\. Bind it to your device[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/setup#2-bind-it-to-your-device "Direct link to 2. Bind it to your device")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In the menu's configuration on the right you'll find:

*   **Menu Availability** — choose **Macro Pad Only** if the menu should exist purely on the device and never appear on screen. Any other availability also works; the menu will then be shown on screen _and_ on the pad.
*   **Macro Pad** — pick your device. Connected pads are listed by name and serial number.

You can bind either to a **specific device** (by serial number) or to **any device of that model**. Model binding is the better choice for presets you want to share, since it doesn't depend on one particular unit's serial number.

3\. Add items[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/setup#3-add-items "Direct link to 3. Add items")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every item of the menu becomes something on the device. Items fill the keys in the normal item order, so the order of your items decides the layout.

That's all — the pad updates as you edit the menu.

Per-app pads[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/setup#per-app-pads "Direct link to Per-app pads")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Menus that are set up for a specific app take priority over global ones, so a pad automatically follows the frontmost application and falls back to your global menu. Create one menu per app, bind them to the same device, and the pad switches by itself.

My device isn't listed[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/setup#my-device-isnt-listed "Direct link to My device isn't listed")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Open the **Macro Pad** dropdown once with the device plugged in — Stream Decks are only initialised when something asks for them.

If it's a **Loupedeck or Razer Stream Controller**, make sure no other software is using it. Loupedeck's own application and Logitech's plugin service hold the connection exclusively, and while either runs BetterTouchTool cannot see the device at all.

If it's a **Logitech MX Creative Keypad**, the same applies to Logi Options+ and its plugin service — quit them first. Also connect the Keypad by USB; it cannot be driven over Bluetooth.

If it still isn't listed, see [Supported Devices](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices)
 — your pad may be a rebadge of a supported design and can be registered manually.

*   [1\. Create a Floating Menu](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/setup#1-create-a-floating-menu)
    
*   [2\. Bind it to your device](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/setup#2-bind-it-to-your-device)
    
*   [3\. Add items](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/setup#3-add-items)
    
*   [Per-app pads](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/setup#per-app-pads)
    
*   [My device isn't listed](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/setup#my-device-isnt-listed)

# BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

BetterTouchTool can drive macro pads directly from a floating menu: your menu items become the keys, knobs and touch strip of the device, with the same look and the same actions you already configure everywhere else.

This page lists the devices BetterTouchTool recognises.

Elgato Stream Deck[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#elgato-stream-deck "Direct link to Elgato Stream Deck")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All Stream Deck models supported by BetterTouchTool's Stream Deck integration can also be used as macro pads, including the Stream Deck + with its knobs and touch strip.

Loupedeck and Razer Stream Controller[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#loupedeck-and-razer-stream-controller "Direct link to Loupedeck and Razer Stream Controller")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

These devices were discontinued after Logitech acquired Loupedeck, and Loupedeck's own software dropped support for the Razer versions in 2026. BetterTouchTool drives them anyway.

| Device | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Loupedeck Live | Tested |
| Razer Stream Controller | Tested |
| Loupedeck Live S | Should work |
| Razer Stream Controller X | Should work |

On the Loupedeck Live and the Razer Stream Controller you get all of it: the 12 touch keys, both side touch strips, the 6 dials (turning **and** pressing) and the 8 round buttons.

The round buttons have no display, so an item placed on one **lights it in the item's own colour** instead of drawing on it.

To use the side strips, set an item's placement to **LCD Strip** — items fill the left strip from top to bottom, then the right one.

The device can only be used by one application at a time

Loupedeck's own software and Logitech's plugin service claim the connection exclusively. If either is running, BetterTouchTool cannot talk to the device at all. Quit them first.

**Loupedeck+ is a different device.** It is screenless and behaves as a MIDI controller, so use BetterTouchTool's MIDI triggers for it instead. Note that "LD-2001" printed on the case belongs to the Loupedeck **Live**, not the Loupedeck+.

Very old firmware (0.2.5 and earlier) used a different display layout and is not supported. BetterTouchTool detects this and leaves the device alone rather than drawing garbage on it.

Logitech MX Creative Console[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#logitech-mx-creative-console "Direct link to Logitech MX Creative Console")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The console is two separate devices, and BetterTouchTool treats them differently.

| Device | Status |
| --- | --- |
| MX Creative Keypad (the half with the 9 screens) | Tested |
| MX Creative Dialpad (the half with the dials) | Tested |

The **Keypad** is a macro pad: its 9 keys show your menu items, exactly like a Stream Deck. The two `<` and `>` buttons below the keys have no display, so set an item's placement to **Buttons Without Display** to put actions on them.

Connect the Keypad with its USB cable — it cannot be driven over Bluetooth.

The **Dialpad** has no screens, so it is not a macro pad. It is configured under [Logitech Mouse Support](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/normal-mouse/logitech#mx-creative-dialpad)
 instead, where its four buttons can be made available for remapping and each of its two dials can be set to scroll or to trigger your own actions.

caution

Quit Logi Options+ before using the Keypad. Logitech's software and its plugin service claim the device exclusively, and BetterTouchTool then cannot talk to it at all.

AJAZZ, Mirabox and related pads[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#ajazz-mirabox-and-related-pads "Direct link to AJAZZ, Mirabox and related pads")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Many of these pads are the same hardware sold under different brand names, so a device that isn't from AJAZZ or Mirabox may still work — look for your model in the lists below.

### Pads with 10 keys, 4 knobs and a touch strip[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#pads-with-10-keys-4-knobs-and-a-touch-strip "Direct link to Pads with 10 keys, 4 knobs and a touch strip")

| Device | Status |
| --- | --- |
| AJAZZ AKP05E | Tested |
| AJAZZ AKP05 | Should work |
| AJAZZ AKP05E Pro | Should work |
| AJAZZ AKP05CN Pro | Should work |
| Mirabox N4 | Should work |
| Mirabox N4E | Should work |
| Mirabox N4 Pro | Should work |
| Mirabox N4 Pro E | Should work |
| VSDInside N4 Pro | Should work |
| Mars Gaming MSD-Pro | Should work |
| Soomfon CN003 | Should work |
| Streonor S10 Pro | Should work |
| Redragon SS552 | Should work |

### Pads with 6 keys, 3 buttons and 3 knobs[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#pads-with-6-keys-3-buttons-and-3-knobs "Direct link to Pads with 6 keys, 3 buttons and 3 knobs")

Tested on hardware. The three plain buttons and the three knobs have no displays; they work like any other item and simply can't show anything.

| Device | Status |
| --- | --- |
| AJAZZ AKP03 | Should work |
| AJAZZ AKP03E | Should work |
| AJAZZ AKP03R | Should work |
| AJAZZ AKP03E (rev. 2) | Should work |
| AJAZZ AKP03R (rev. 2) | Should work |
| Mirabox N3 | Should work |
| Mirabox N3EN | Should work |
| Mirabox N3CN3 | Should work |
| Soomfon SE | Should work |
| TreasLin N3 | Tested |
| Redragon SS551 | Should work |
| Mars Gaming MSD TWO | Should work |

### Pads with 15 keys and a side display strip[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#pads-with-15-keys-and-a-side-display-strip "Direct link to Pads with 15 keys and a side display strip")

Tested on hardware (AKP153 rev. 2). Alongside the 15 keys these have a narrow LCD strip down the side, split into three segments. Place items on it by setting their placement to **LCD Strip**. The segments appear to be display-only — they show what you put there, but pressing them does nothing.

| Device | Status |
| --- | --- |
| AJAZZ AKP153E (rev. 2) | Tested |
| AJAZZ AKP153R (rev. 2) | Should work |
| KUIYN and other rebadges of the above | Should work |

### Pads with 15 keys and 3 buttons[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#pads-with-15-keys-and-3-buttons "Direct link to Pads with 15 keys and 3 buttons")

| Device | Status |
| --- | --- |
| VSD Inside M18 | Should work |
| Mirabox M18 | Should work |
| Mirabox M18EN | Should work |

Not yet supported[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#not-yet-supported "Direct link to Not yet supported")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   **The older AJAZZ AKP153 / AKP153E / AKP153R and Mirabox HSV293S** — the first hardware revision is recognised but not finished, and keys are likely to appear in the wrong order. The **rev. 2** models listed above do work. If your AKP153 is detected but scrambled, you have a first-revision unit.
*   **Ulanzi D200 / D200H** — a different kind of device that needs separate support.

Every model BetterTouchTool recognises[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#every-model-bettertouchtool-recognises "Direct link to Every model BetterTouchTool recognises")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Most of these pads are a handful of designs sold under many brand names, so it is worth searching this list for your exact model. Every name below is recognised by name and USB id; see the sections above for what each family can do.

**Logitech** — MX Creative Keypad, MX Creative Dialpad

**Loupedeck / Razer** — Loupedeck Live, Loupedeck Live S, Razer Stream Controller, Razer Stream Controller X

**Elgato** — Stream Deck, Stream Deck Mini, Stream Deck XL, Stream Deck Neo, Stream Deck +, Stream Deck Pedal

**AJAZZ** — AKP03, AKP03E, AKP03R, AKP03E (rev. 2), AKP03R (rev. 2), AKP05, AKP05E, AKP05E Pro, AKP05CN Pro, AKP153, AKP153E, AKP153R, AKP153E (rev. 2), AKP153R (rev. 2)

**Mirabox** — N3, N3EN, N3CN3, N4, N4E, N4 Pro, N4 Pro E, M18, M18EN, HSV293S

**Other brands on the same hardware** — VSDInside N4 Pro, VSD Inside M18, Basicolor / VSDInside HSV293S, Mars Gaming MSD-Pro, Mars Gaming MSD TWO, Soomfon CN003, Soomfon SE, Streonor S10 Pro, TreasLin N3, Redragon SS551, Redragon SS552, KUIYN

If your pad is not in this list it may still be the same hardware under yet another badge — see [My pad is the same hardware but isn't recognised](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#my-pad-is-the-same-hardware-but-isnt-recognised)
 to register it yourself.

What "Should work" means[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#what-should-work-means "Direct link to What "Should work" means")

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The AJAZZ AKP05E, the AKP153 rev. 2, the AKP03/N3 family, the Loupedeck Live and the Razer Stream Controller have been tested on real hardware. The other pads use the same designs and are expected to work, but they haven't been confirmed yet — if you own one, feedback is very welcome.

My pad isn't listed or isn't detected[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#my-pad-isnt-listed-or-isnt-detected "Direct link to My pad isn't listed or isn't detected")

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If your pad looks like one of the devices above but isn't picked up, it may be the same hardware with a different identifier. To report it:

1.  Open **System Information** (hold ⌥ and choose → System Information).
2.  Select **USB** in the sidebar and find your pad in the list.
3.  Note its **Vendor ID** and **Product ID** (for example `0x0300` and `0x3004`), along with the exact product name.

Send those along with the brand and model, and support can usually be added.

My pad is the same hardware but isn't recognised[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/supported-devices#my-pad-is-the-same-hardware-but-isnt-recognised "Direct link to My pad is the same hardware but isn't recognised")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Most of these pads are a handful of designs sold under many brand names, so an unlisted device is usually one of the families above with a different identifier. You can register it yourself, without waiting for a new version.

Find the Vendor and Product ID as described above, then run this in Terminal (quit BetterTouchTool first), using the family your pad matches:

    defaults write com.hegenberg.BetterTouchTool BTTMacroPadExtraDevices -array \  "0x0300:0x3010:akp153v3:My Macro Pad"

*   The first two values are the Vendor ID and Product ID.
*   The third is the family: `akp05` (10 keys, 4 knobs, touch strip), `akp03` (6 keys, 3 buttons, 3 knobs), `m18` (15 keys, 3 buttons) or `akp153` (15 keys + side strip). If your pad is a newer revision try `akp153v3`, and for older AKP03-style pads `akp03v2`.
*   The fourth is any name you like, shown in BetterTouchTool.

Start BetterTouchTool again and the pad should be listed. If it is detected but keys appear in the wrong order, it is a different family — try another one, and please report what worked so it can be added properly.

# BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/actions#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

These actions can be assigned to any trigger — a keyboard shortcut, a gesture, or an item on the pad itself. You'll find them in the **Macro Pad Actions** group when choosing an action.

Switching what a pad shows[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/actions#switching-what-a-pad-shows "Direct link to Switching what a pad shows")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   **Macro Pad: Show Menu** — points a pad at a different Floating Menu, by name or UUID. Leave the name empty to send the pad back to the menu it is bound to.
*   **Open Specific Submenu in Floating Menu** — opens a submenu. This also works for on-screen menus, so one action covers both.
*   **Floating Menu: Close Submenu** — leaves the current submenu.
*   **Macro Pad: Next Page / Previous Page** — page navigation.

Together these replace the older _Open / Close Stream Deck Group_ triggers.

Display and power[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/actions#display-and-power "Direct link to Display and power")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   **Macro Pad: Set Brightness** and **Macro Pad: Change Brightness**
*   **Macro Pad: Turn On**, **Turn Off** and **Toggle On/Off**

These work with Elgato Stream Decks as well as AJAZZ/Mirabox and Loupedeck/Razer pads.

Choosing which device is affected[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/actions#choosing-which-device-is-affected "Direct link to Choosing which device is affected")

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Actions that can target a device have a field for a serial number. Leave it empty to affect **every** macro pad driven by a Floating Menu, or enter a serial to affect one. The currently connected pads and their serial numbers are listed below the field, so you can copy the right one.

*   [Switching what a pad shows](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/actions#switching-what-a-pad-shows)
    
*   [Display and power](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/actions#display-and-power)
    
*   [Choosing which device is affected](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/macro-pads/actions#choosing-which-device-is-affected)

# BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

The simplest way to create a BetterTouchTool plugin. Write a single `.swift` file, drop it into the Plugins folder, and BTT compiles and loads it automatically - no Xcode project required.

Requirements[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#requirements "Direct link to Requirements")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   Xcode Command Line Tools must be installed: `xcode-select --install`

How It Works[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#how-it-works "Direct link to How It Works")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  Create a `.swift` file containing your plugin class
2.  Drop it onto the BTT preferences window, or copy it to either `~/Library/Application Support/BetterTouchTool/Plugins/` or `/Library/Application Support/BetterTouchTool/Plugins/`
3.  BTT detects the file and asks: _"Compile & Load?"_
4.  On approval, BTT compiles it with `swiftc` into a plugin bundle
5.  The plugin becomes available immediately

If you edit the `.swift` file, BTT detects the change and offers to recompile. Deleting the `.swift` file automatically removes the compiled bundle.

Metadata Comments[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#metadata-comments "Direct link to Metadata Comments")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Put metadata comments in the first 50 lines of your file. Set an explicit, stable identifier so renaming the file does not change the plugin identity:

    // BTT-Plugin-Name: My Widget// BTT-Plugin-Identifier: com.myname.mywidget// BTT-Plugin-Type: FloatingMenuWidget// BTT-Plugin-Icon: star.fill

| Comment | Description | Default if omitted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BTT-Plugin-Name` | Display name in BTT | Filename without extension |
| `BTT-Plugin-Identifier` | Unique reverse-domain identifier | `com.btt.swift.<filename>` |
| `BTT-Plugin-Type` | Plugin type | Inferred from protocol conformance |
| `BTT-Plugin-Icon` | SF Symbol name for the icon | None |

Supported `BTT-Plugin-Type` values: `FloatingMenuWidget`, `Action`, `StreamDeck`, `TouchBar`, `Trigger`, `Launcher`

Protocols and Bridging Header[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#protocols-and-bridging-header "Direct link to Protocols and Bridging Header")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All plugin protocols are defined in `BTTSwiftPluginHeader.h`, shipped inside the BTT app bundle. The bridging header is automatically provided during compilation - you don't need to import it manually. Use the protocols, models, delegates and form constants exposed by that header, together with the installed macOS SDK. BTT app internals such as `LauncherStore`, `APPDEL` and internal SwiftUI modifiers are not plugin APIs.

Keep the principal declaration on one line, for example `class MyWidget: NSObject, BTTFloatingMenuWidgetInterface`. The source metadata parser uses that declaration to discover your class. Let Swift provide its module-qualified Objective-C name; a custom `@objc(Name)` can conflict with the previous version during hot reload.

Callback Signatures[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#callback-signatures "Direct link to Callback Signatures")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Use the exact Swift signatures imported from BTT's header. Untyped Objective-C dictionaries use `AnyHashable` keys:

| Plugin type | Configuration parameter |
| --- | --- |
| Floating Menu Widget, Launcher, Trigger | `[AnyHashable: Any]?` in `didReceiveNewConfigurationValues(_:)` |
| Stream Deck, Touch Bar | `[AnyHashable: Any]` in `didReceiveNewConfigurationValues(_:)` |
| Action | `[AnyHashable: Any]?` in `executeAction(withConfiguration:completionBlock:)` |

A warning that a method “nearly matches” an optional protocol requirement means BTT may never call that method. Correct the signature; do not hide the warning by making the method private. Builds containing this warning are rejected by BTT's updated plugin compiler, leaving the previous compiled bundle intact. Older BTT builds may accept the warning, so check diagnostics when supporting older installations.

Keep AppKit and SwiftUI updates on the main thread. Move blocking work out of callbacks, preserve stable item IDs, and release timers and observers when the plugin stops or its view disappears.

Creating and Editing With AI[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#creating-and-editing-with-ai "Direct link to Creating and Editing With AI")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Use the **BTT Plugin Creator / Editor** skills and retrieve the reference for the intended plugin type before generating code. The [AI authoring workflow](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/ai-authoring)
 lists the matching tools.

For a new Swift plugin, pass `source_code` and `plugin_file_name` directly to `compile_swift_plugin`. For an existing plugin, read its source, make focused edits with the available file tools, then compile with `swift_file_path`. Preserve literal backslashes and Swift interpolation when moving source through JSON or JavaScript.

The compile tool manages its file-watcher suppression. A `BTT-AI-Managed` comment has no effect on the current loader. A `SUCCESS:` result confirms compilation and loading; verify the configured plugin's behavior separately.

Examples by Plugin Type[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#examples-by-plugin-type "Direct link to Examples by Plugin Type")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Floating Menu Widget[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#floating-menu-widget "Direct link to Floating Menu Widget")

    // BTT-Plugin-Name: Hello Widget// BTT-Plugin-Identifier: com.example.hellowidget// BTT-Plugin-Type: FloatingMenuWidget// BTT-Plugin-Icon: hand.wave.fillimport Cocoaclass HelloWidget: NSObject, BTTFloatingMenuWidgetInterface {    weak var delegate: (any BTTFloatingMenuWidgetDelegate)?    static func widgetName() -> String { "Hello Widget" }    static func widgetDescription() -> String { "A simple greeting widget" }    static func widgetIcon() -> String { "hand.wave.fill" }    // Override the menu item's configured size (optional)    static func widgetMinWidth() -> CGFloat { 200 }    static func widgetMinHeight() -> CGFloat { 80 }    func makeWidgetView() -> NSView {        let label = NSTextField(labelWithString: "Hello from BTT!")        label.font = .systemFont(ofSize: 24, weight: .medium)        label.textColor = .white        return label    }    func widgetDidAppear() {}    func widgetWillDisappear() {}}

See [Floating Menu Widget Plugins](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget)
 for the full protocol reference, SwiftUI support, and custom action categories.

### Stream Deck[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#stream-deck "Direct link to Stream Deck")

    // BTT-Plugin-Name: Counter// BTT-Plugin-Identifier: com.example.counter// BTT-Plugin-Type: StreamDeck// BTT-Plugin-Icon: number.circle.fillimport Cocoaclass Counter: NSObject, BTTStreamDeckPluginInterface {    weak var delegate: (any BTTStreamDeckPluginDelegate)?    private var count = 0    static func configurationFormItems() -> BTTPluginFormItem? { nil }    func widgetTitleStrings() -> [String]? {        return ["\(count)"]    }    func buttonDown(_ identifier: String) -> Bool {        count += 1        delegate?.requestUpdate(self)        return false // return true to cancel assigned BTT actions    }    func buttonUp(_ identifier: String) -> Bool {        return false    }}

See [Stream Deck Plugins](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck)
 for the full protocol reference and all rendering options.

### Touch Bar[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#touch-bar "Direct link to Touch Bar")

    // BTT-Plugin-Name: Clock Text// BTT-Plugin-Identifier: com.example.clocktext// BTT-Plugin-Type: TouchBar// BTT-Plugin-Icon: clockimport Cocoaclass ClockText: NSObject, BTTPluginInterface {    weak var delegate: (any BTTTouchBarPluginDelegate)?    static func configurationFormItems() -> BTTPluginFormItem? { nil }    func touchBarTitleString() -> String? {        let formatter = DateFormatter()        formatter.dateFormat = "HH:mm:ss"        return formatter.string(from: Date())    }}

See [Touch Bar Plugins](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/touch-bar)
 for the full protocol reference and all rendering options.

### Action[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#action "Direct link to Action")

    // BTT-Plugin-Name: Show Greeting// BTT-Plugin-Identifier: com.example.showgreeting// BTT-Plugin-Type: Action// BTT-Plugin-Icon: bubble.left.fillimport Cocoaclass ShowGreeting: NSObject, BTTActionPluginInterface {    weak var delegate: (any BTTActionPluginDelegate)?    static func configurationFormItems() -> BTTPluginFormItem? { nil }    func executeAction(        withConfiguration config: [AnyHashable: Any]?,        completionBlock: ((@Sendable (Any?) -> Void)?)    ) {        let alert = NSAlert()        alert.messageText = "Hello from a BTT Action Plugin!"        alert.runModal()        completionBlock?("done")    }}

See [Action Plugins](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/action)
 for the full protocol reference.

### Trigger[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#trigger "Direct link to Trigger")

    // BTT-Plugin-Name: Clipboard Change// BTT-Plugin-Identifier: com.example.clipboardchangetrigger// BTT-Plugin-Type: Trigger// BTT-Plugin-Icon: doc.on.clipboardimport Cocoaclass ClipboardChangeTrigger: NSObject, BTTTriggerPluginInterface {    weak var delegate: (any BTTTriggerPluginDelegate)?    private var timer: Timer?    private var lastChangeCount = NSPasteboard.general.changeCount    static func triggerName() -> String { "Clipboard Change" }    static func triggerDescription() -> String { "Fires when clipboard content changes" }    static func triggerIcon() -> String { "doc.on.clipboard" }    static func configurationFormItems() -> BTTPluginFormItem? { nil }    func didReceiveNewConfigurationValues(_ config: [AnyHashable: Any]?) {}    func startObserving() {        stopObserving()        lastChangeCount = NSPasteboard.general.changeCount        timer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 1.0, repeats: true) { [weak self] _ in            guard let self else { return }            let current = NSPasteboard.general.changeCount            if current != self.lastChangeCount {                self.lastChangeCount = current                let content = NSPasteboard.general.string(forType: .string) ?? ""                self.delegate?.triggerFired(self, withContext: ["clipboardContent": content])            }        }    }    func stopObserving() {        timer?.invalidate()        timer = nil    }}

See [Trigger Plugins](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/trigger)
 for the full protocol reference, lifecycle management, and more examples.

### Launcher[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#launcher "Direct link to Launcher")

    // BTT-Plugin-Name: Demo Launcher Plugin// BTT-Plugin-Identifier: com.example.demolauncherplugin// BTT-Plugin-Type: Launcher// BTT-Plugin-Icon: sparkles.rectangle.stackimport AppKitimport SwiftUIclass DemoLauncherPlugin: NSObject, BTTLauncherPluginInterface {    weak var delegate: (any BTTLauncherPluginDelegate)?    static func launcherPluginName() -> String { "Demo Launcher Plugin" }    static func launcherPluginDescription() -> String { "Shows custom launcher results" }    static func launcherPluginIcon() -> String { "sparkles.rectangle.stack" }    func launcherResults(for context: BTTLauncherPluginContext) -> [BTTLauncherPluginResult]? {        let result = BTTLauncherPluginResult()        result.itemIdentifier = "demo-root"        result.title = "Launcher Plugin Demo"        result.subtitle = "Returned by a native launcher plugin"        result.systemImageName = "sparkles.rectangle.stack"        result.surfaceIdentifier = "demo-surface"        return [result]    }    func launcherSurface(        forItemIdentifier itemIdentifier: String,        surfaceIdentifier: String?,        context: BTTLauncherPluginContext    ) -> (any BTTLauncherPluginSurfaceInterface)? {        DemoLauncherSurface()    }}final class DemoLauncherSurface: NSObject, BTTLauncherPluginSurfaceInterface {    func makeLauncherSurfaceView() -> NSView {        NSHostingView(rootView: DemoLauncherSurfaceView())    }}struct DemoLauncherSurfaceView: View {    var body: some View {        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10) {            Label("Hello from a launcher surface", systemImage: "sparkles.rectangle.stack")                .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))            Text("This view is rendered with SwiftUI and hosted inside the BetterTouchTool Launcher.")                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)        }        .padding(24)        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading)    }}

See [Launcher Plugins](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/launcher)
 for the full protocol reference, commands, launcher surfaces, context values, and Xcode bundle setup.

BTT Variable Access[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#btt-variable-access "Direct link to BTT Variable Access")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All plugin types have access to BTT variables through their delegate:

    // Set a variable (accessible as {variable_name} throughout BTT)delegate?.setVariable("my_var", value: "hello")// Read a variablelet value = delegate?.getVariable("my_var")

Adding Configuration Forms[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/swift-source-plugins#adding-configuration-forms "Direct link to Adding Configuration Forms")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Any Swift source plugin can include user-configurable settings by implementing `configurationFormItems()`. This fragment uses the nullable callback for a floating-menu widget; choose the signature from the table above for other types:

    static func configurationFormItems() -> BTTPluginFormItem? {    let group = BTTPluginFormItem()    group.formFieldType = BTTFormTypeFormGroup    let textField = BTTPluginFormItem()    textField.formFieldType = BTTFormTypeTextField    textField.formLabel1 = "Label Text"    textField.formFieldID = "labelText"    textField.defaultValue = "Hello!"    group.formOptions = [textField]    return group}func didReceiveNewConfigurationValues(_ configurationValues: [AnyHashable: Any]?) {    // Values arrive with a "plugin_var_" prefix on the formFieldID    if let text = configurationValues?["plugin_var_labelText"] as? String {        labelText = text    }}

Use plain field IDs in `configurationFormItems()`, for example `labelText`; BTT applies the `plugin_var_` prefix when saving and delivering configuration values. For trigger plugins, configuration is saved per configured BTT trigger instance and is delivered before `startObserving()` runs.

See the [Configuration Forms Reference](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/configuration-forms)
 for all available field types.

# BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/webview/config#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Configuration Options[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/webview/config#configuration-options "Direct link to Configuration Options")

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Most of the configuration options you see when clicking the config tab should be self-explanatory, but let's have a quick look: ![mcc](https://docs.folivora.ai/assets/images/webviewconfig-371ee5558f3825593b1b7a5a551df632.png)

*   **Width/Height** - The size of the webview
    
*   **Resizable** - when activated the webview allows to be resized by dragging the edges/corners like normal windows. Known issue: the resize cursor might not show up, you'll still be able to resize.
    
*   **Center on Monitor With Mouse (Default)**: Will center the floating webview on the monitor that currently contains the mouse cursor.
    
*   **Specify Position**: Various options on where to place the webview.
    
*   **Update above position & size after manually moving or resizing**: This will automatically save & restore the latest position & size if you have moved the webview around.
    
*   **Use White Background**: This will make the background of the webview white. By default it is transparent and you can set the background color using css. In some cases (e.g. for external websites) you might not want the transparent background.
    
*   **Show Window Buttons**: By default the webview doesn't show the window buttons on the top left. This checkbox enables them.
    
*   **Draw Title Bar Bezel**: By default the webview doesn't have a title bar. This checkbox enables that (e.g. for easier dragging).
    
*   **Close When Clicking Outside**: Will close the webview as soon as clicking on some other window. Known issue: might not work while BTT preferences are open.
    
*   **Show BTT Dock Icon**: This will show the BTT icon in the Dock while the webview is active. It will make the webview active when clicked.
    
*   **Z-Index**: Using this you can select the window level for the webview. By default it is floating on top of all other windows. You can also stick it to the desktop, so it will only be visible when showing the desktop. You can also specify a custom NSWindowLevel number, see [](http://www.gietal.net/blog/nswindowlevel-shenanigans)
    [http://www.gietal.net/blog/nswindowlevel-shenanigans](http://www.gietal.net/blog/nswindowlevel-shenanigans)
    

Advanced[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/webview/config#advanced "Direct link to Advanced")

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![mcc](https://docs.folivora.ai/assets/images/webview_advanced-be909821153e5d4450d319c950947a33.png)

*   **Do NOT keep content active in background**: By default the webview only loads the web content once and then keeps it active in the background. This might not be wanted for various reasons. For example you might not want to have music playing while the webview is hidden.
    
*   **Custom User Agent**: Allows you to set a custom user agent. Can be helpful in order to get a smaller mobile version of a website.
    
*   **Open URLs with prefix in System Browser**: You might want to open http links in the system browser.
    
*   **Move Window by dragging content**: This allows to move the webview by dragging the web content. This can result in unwanted clicks, thus might not work on all websites. Use "only move while holding CMD" to prevent accidental clicks.
    

Security:[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/webview/config#security "Direct link to Security:")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   **Shared Secret**: The shared secret is only necessary if you load a website from an external server and that website tries to trigger functions within BTT.

*   [Configuration Options](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/webview/config#configuration-options)
    
*   [Advanced](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/webview/config#advanced)
    
*   [Security:](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/webview/config#security)

# Touch Bar Plugins | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/touch-bar#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Touch Bar plugins render custom widgets on the MacBook Pro Touch Bar. They conform to the `BTTPluginInterface` protocol and use the `.btttouchbarplugin` bundle extension for Xcode projects.

Protocol: `BTTPluginInterface`[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/touch-bar#protocol-bttplugininterface "Direct link to protocol-bttplugininterface")

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Rendering Options[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/touch-bar#rendering-options "Direct link to Rendering Options")

Implement **one** of the following three methods. If multiple are implemented, BTT uses the first one found in this order:

#### Option 1: Return a String[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/touch-bar#option-1-return-a-string "Direct link to Option 1: Return a String")

The simplest option. BTT renders the string using its standard Touch Bar widget styling, so all user-configured appearance properties (background color, font, etc.) are applied.

    func touchBarTitleString() -> String? {    let formatter = DateFormatter()    formatter.dateFormat = "HH:mm:ss"    return formatter.string(from: Date())}

#### Option 2: Return an NSButton[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/touch-bar#option-2-return-an-nsbutton "Direct link to Option 2: Return an NSButton")

Return a custom `NSButton` instance for full control over the button appearance. **Always return the same instance** - do not create a new button on each call.

    private lazy var button: NSButton = {    let btn = NSButton(title: "Click Me", target: nil, action: nil)    btn.bezelColor = .systemBlue    return btn}()func touchBarButton() -> NSButton? {    return button}

#### Option 3: Return an NSViewController[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/touch-bar#option-3-return-an-nsviewcontroller "Direct link to Option 3: Return an NSViewController")

Return a custom view controller for complete control over the widget's view hierarchy. **Always return the same instance.**

    private lazy var viewController: NSViewController = {    let vc = NSViewController()    let view = NSView(frame: NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 40, height: 30))    view.wantsLayer = true    view.layer?.backgroundColor = NSColor.systemRed.cgColor    view.layer?.cornerRadius = 8    vc.view = view    return vc}()func touchBarViewController() -> NSViewController? {    return viewController}

### Configuration[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/touch-bar#configuration "Direct link to Configuration")

    // Optional: return form items for the BTT sidebarstatic func configurationFormItems() -> BTTPluginFormItem? { nil }// Called when the user changes configuration valuesfunc didReceiveNewConfigurationValues(_ configurationValues: [AnyHashable: Any]) {    // Apply saved values to your retained view or model here.}

See the [Configuration Forms Reference](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/configuration-forms)
 for available field types.

### Delegate Methods[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/touch-bar#delegate-methods "Direct link to Delegate Methods")

The `delegate` property (type `BTTTouchBarPluginDelegate`) provides:

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `executeAssignedBTTActions(_:)` | Execute the BTT actions assigned to this widget |
| `update(with:sender:)` | Update the widget's displayed title |
| `setVariable(_:value:)` | Set a BTT variable |
| `getVariable(_:)` | Read a BTT variable |

Complete Example[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/touch-bar#complete-example "Direct link to Complete Example")

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A Touch Bar widget that shows a configurable label and executes assigned actions when tapped:

    // BTT-Plugin-Name: Configurable Label// BTT-Plugin-Identifier: com.example.configurablelabel// BTT-Plugin-Type: TouchBar// BTT-Plugin-Icon: textformatimport Cocoaclass ConfigurableLabel: NSObject, BTTPluginInterface {    weak var delegate: (any BTTTouchBarPluginDelegate)?    private var labelText = "Hello"    static func configurationFormItems() -> BTTPluginFormItem? {        let group = BTTPluginFormItem()        group.formFieldType = BTTFormTypeFormGroup        let textField = BTTPluginFormItem()        textField.formFieldType = BTTFormTypeTextField        textField.formLabel1 = "Label Text"        textField.formFieldID = "labelText"        textField.defaultValue = "Hello"        group.formOptions = [textField]        return group    }    func didReceiveNewConfigurationValues(_ configurationValues: [AnyHashable: Any]) {        if let text = configurationValues["plugin_var_labelText"] as? String {            labelText = text        }        delegate?.update(with: labelText, sender: self)    }    func touchBarTitleString() -> String? {        return labelText    }}

Xcode Bundle Setup[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/touch-bar#xcode-bundle-setup "Direct link to Xcode Bundle Setup")

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For Xcode-based Touch Bar plugins, the bundle extension is `.btttouchbarplugin`. Set these `Info.plist` keys:

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `BTTPluginType` | `TouchBar` |
| `NSPrincipalClass` | `$(PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME).YourClassName` |

See [Xcode Bundle Plugins & Distribution](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/xcode-bundle-distribution)
 for the full setup process.

# Floating Menu Widget Plugins | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Floating Menu Widget plugins embed custom native views into floating menus and desktop widgets. They conform to the `BTTFloatingMenuWidgetInterface` protocol and use the `.bttwidget` bundle extension for Xcode projects.

Plugin widgets appear as a dedicated item type when configuring a floating menu. They are rendered natively, so they have full access to macOS APIs and deliver smooth, high-performance UI.

Protocol: `BTTFloatingMenuWidgetInterface`[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#protocol-bttfloatingmenuwidgetinterface "Direct link to protocol-bttfloatingmenuwidgetinterface")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Required Method[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#required-method "Direct link to Required Method")

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `makeWidgetView() -> NSView` | Return the view to display in the floating menu |

### Optional Class Methods[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#optional-class-methods "Direct link to Optional Class Methods")

| Method | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `widgetName() -> String` | Display name in BTT | Plugin name |
| `widgetDescription() -> String` | Short description | None |
| `widgetIcon() -> String` | SF Symbol name | None |
| `widgetWantsInteractiveView() -> Bool` | Set to `true` if the widget has its own clickable controls (buttons, sliders, etc.). When `false`, BTT handles click events for action assignment. | `false` |
| `widgetMinWidth() -> CGFloat` | Minimum width override | Item's configured size |
| `widgetMinHeight() -> CGFloat` | Minimum height override | Item's configured size |
| `widgetMaxWidth() -> CGFloat` | Maximum width override | Item's configured size |
| `widgetMaxHeight() -> CGFloat` | Maximum height override | Item's configured size |
| `configurationFormItems() -> BTTPluginFormItem?` | Configuration form for the BTT sidebar | None |
| `additionalActionCategories() -> [[AnyHashable: Any]]?` | Custom action categories | None |

### Optional Instance Methods[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#optional-instance-methods "Direct link to Optional Instance Methods")

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `widgetDidAppear()` | Called when the widget becomes visible |
| `widgetWillDisappear()` | Called when the widget is about to be hidden |
| `didReceiveNewConfigurationValues(_:)` | Called when the user changes configuration values |

Simple Widget (AppKit)[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#simple-widget-appkit "Direct link to Simple Widget (AppKit)")

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    // BTT-Plugin-Name: Hello Widget// BTT-Plugin-Identifier: com.example.hellowidget// BTT-Plugin-Type: FloatingMenuWidget// BTT-Plugin-Icon: hand.wave.fillimport Cocoaclass HelloWidget: NSObject, BTTFloatingMenuWidgetInterface {    weak var delegate: (any BTTFloatingMenuWidgetDelegate)?    static func widgetName() -> String { "Hello Widget" }    static func widgetDescription() -> String { "A simple greeting widget" }    static func widgetIcon() -> String { "hand.wave.fill" }    // Override the menu item's configured size (optional)    static func widgetMinWidth() -> CGFloat { 200 }    static func widgetMinHeight() -> CGFloat { 80 }    func makeWidgetView() -> NSView {        let label = NSTextField(labelWithString: "Hello from BTT!")        label.font = .systemFont(ofSize: 24, weight: .medium)        label.textColor = .white        return label    }    func widgetDidAppear() {}    func widgetWillDisappear() {}}

Interactive Widget (SwiftUI)[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#interactive-widget-swiftui "Direct link to Interactive Widget (SwiftUI)")

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For richer UI, use SwiftUI by wrapping your view in an `NSHostingView`. If your widget contains interactive controls, return `true` from `widgetWantsInteractiveView()` so BTT doesn't intercept clicks.

    // BTT-Plugin-Name: Timer Widget// BTT-Plugin-Identifier: com.example.timerwidget// BTT-Plugin-Type: FloatingMenuWidget// BTT-Plugin-Icon: timerimport Cocoaimport SwiftUIclass TimerWidget: NSObject, BTTFloatingMenuWidgetInterface {    weak var delegate: (any BTTFloatingMenuWidgetDelegate)?    static func widgetName() -> String { "Timer Widget" }    static func widgetDescription() -> String { "A simple countdown timer" }    static func widgetIcon() -> String { "timer" }    static func widgetWantsInteractiveView() -> Bool { true }    static func widgetMinWidth() -> CGFloat { 250 }    static func widgetMinHeight() -> CGFloat { 150 }    static func widgetMaxWidth() -> CGFloat { 300 }    static func widgetMaxHeight() -> CGFloat { 200 }    func makeWidgetView() -> NSView {        return NSHostingView(rootView: TimerView())    }}struct TimerView: View {    @State private var secondsLeft = 60    @State private var running = false    var body: some View {        VStack(spacing: 12) {            Text("\(secondsLeft)s")                .font(.system(size: 48, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))                .monospacedDigit()                .foregroundColor(secondsLeft <= 10 ? .red : .white)            HStack(spacing: 16) {                Button(running ? "Stop" : "Start") {                    running.toggle()                }                Button("Reset") {                    running = false                    secondsLeft = 60                }            }        }        .padding()        .onReceive(            Timer.publish(every: 1, on: .main, in: .common).autoconnect()        ) { _ in            guard running, secondsLeft > 0 else { return }            secondsLeft -= 1            if secondsLeft == 0 { running = false }        }    }}

Configuration Forms[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#configuration-forms "Direct link to Configuration Forms")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Add a custom configuration UI that appears in the BTT sidebar when the user selects the widget:

    // BTT-Plugin-Name: Greeting Widget// BTT-Plugin-Identifier: com.example.greetingwidget// BTT-Plugin-Type: FloatingMenuWidget// BTT-Plugin-Icon: text.bubble.fillimport Cocoaimport SwiftUIclass GreetingWidget: NSObject, BTTFloatingMenuWidgetInterface {    weak var delegate: (any BTTFloatingMenuWidgetDelegate)?    private var greetingText = "Hello!"    private var fontSize: Double = 24    private let label = NSTextField(labelWithString: "")    static func widgetName() -> String { "Greeting Widget" }    static func widgetDescription() -> String { "A configurable greeting" }    static func widgetIcon() -> String { "text.bubble.fill" }    static func configurationFormItems() -> BTTPluginFormItem? {        let group = BTTPluginFormItem()        group.formFieldType = BTTFormTypeFormGroup        let textField = BTTPluginFormItem()        textField.formFieldType = BTTFormTypeTextField        textField.formLabel1 = "Greeting Text"        textField.formFieldID = "greetingText"        textField.defaultValue = "Hello!"        let sizeSlider = BTTPluginFormItem()        sizeSlider.formFieldType = BTTFormTypeSlider        sizeSlider.formLabel1 = "Font Size"        sizeSlider.formFieldID = "fontSize"        sizeSlider.minValue = NSNumber(value: 10)        sizeSlider.maxValue = NSNumber(value: 72)        sizeSlider.defaultValue = NSNumber(value: 24)        sizeSlider.dataType = BTTFormDataNumber        group.formOptions = [textField, sizeSlider]        return group    }    func didReceiveNewConfigurationValues(_ configurationValues: [AnyHashable: Any]?) {        if let text = configurationValues?["plugin_var_greetingText"] as? String {            greetingText = text        }        if let size = configurationValues?["plugin_var_fontSize"] as? Double {            fontSize = size        }        updateLabel()        delegate?.requestWidgetUpdate(self)    }    private func updateLabel() {        label.stringValue = greetingText        label.font = .systemFont(ofSize: CGFloat(fontSize), weight: .medium)        label.textColor = .labelColor    }    func makeWidgetView() -> NSView {        updateLabel()        return label    }}

The example keeps the label alive and applies configuration changes directly to it before requesting an update. Use the same pattern for an observable SwiftUI model.

See the [Configuration Forms Reference](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/configuration-forms)
 for all available field types.

Custom Action Categories[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#custom-action-categories "Direct link to Custom Action Categories")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

By default, actions assigned to a widget item are executed when clicked. You can define additional action categories so your widget can trigger different sets of user-configured actions for different events - for example, "On Minute Change" or "On Play".

    static func additionalActionCategories() -> [[AnyHashable: Any]]? {    return [        [            "CategoryActionName": "On Minute Change",            "CategoryTag": NSNumber(value: 1000),            "CategoryIconName": "clock.badge",            "CategoryColor": NSColor.systemTeal        ],        [            "CategoryActionName": "On Hour Change",            "CategoryTag": NSNumber(value: 1001),            "CategoryIconName": "clock.arrow.2.circlepath",            "CategoryColor": NSColor.systemOrange        ]    ]}

The custom categories appear in the BTT sidebar when the user configures this widget item. To fire a category from your code:

    delegate?.executeActionCategory(1000, forSender: self)

### Action Category Dictionary Keys[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#action-category-dictionary-keys "Direct link to Action Category Dictionary Keys")

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CategoryActionName` | `String` | Name displayed in the BTT sidebar |
| `CategoryTag` | `NSNumber` | Unique numeric tag (use values 1000+). Pass this to `executeActionCategory(_:forSender:)` to trigger the category. |
| `CategoryIconName` | `String` | SF Symbol name for the category icon (optional) |
| `CategoryColor` | `NSColor` | Tint color for the category in the sidebar (optional) |

Delegate Methods[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#delegate-methods "Direct link to Delegate Methods")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The `delegate` property (type `BTTFloatingMenuWidgetDelegate`) provides:

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `executeAssignedBTTActions(_:)` | Execute the BTT actions assigned to this widget |
| `requestWidgetUpdate(_:)` | Request a refresh after updating the retained view or model; this does not recreate the view |
| `setVariable(_:value:)` | Set a BTT variable |
| `getVariable(_:)` | Read a BTT variable |
| `executeNamedTrigger(_:)` | Execute a named trigger configured in BTT |
| `executeActionCategory(_:forSender:)` | Execute a plugin-defined action category |

Xcode Bundle Setup[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#xcode-bundle-setup "Direct link to Xcode Bundle Setup")

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For Xcode-based floating menu widget plugins, the bundle extension is `.bttwidget`. Set these `Info.plist` keys:

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `BTTPluginType` | `FloatingMenuWidget` |
| `NSPrincipalClass` | `$(PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME).YourClassName` |

See [Xcode Bundle Plugins & Distribution](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/xcode-bundle-distribution)
 for the full setup process.

*   [Protocol: `BTTFloatingMenuWidgetInterface`](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#protocol-bttfloatingmenuwidgetinterface)
    *   [Required Method](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#required-method)
        
    *   [Optional Class Methods](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#optional-class-methods)
        
    *   [Optional Instance Methods](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#optional-instance-methods)
        
*   [Simple Widget (AppKit)](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#simple-widget-appkit)
    
*   [Interactive Widget (SwiftUI)](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#interactive-widget-swiftui)
    
*   [Configuration Forms](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#configuration-forms)
    
*   [Custom Action Categories](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#custom-action-categories)
    *   [Action Category Dictionary Keys](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/floating-menu-widget#action-category-dictionary-keys)

# Stream Deck Plugins | BetterTouchTool Documentation

[Skip to main content](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#__docusaurus_skipToContent_fallback)

On this page

Stream Deck plugins render custom widgets on Elgato Stream Deck buttons. They conform to the `BTTStreamDeckPluginInterface` protocol and use the `.bttstreamdeckplugin` bundle extension for Xcode projects.

Protocol: `BTTStreamDeckPluginInterface`[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#protocol-bttstreamdeckplugininterface "Direct link to protocol-bttstreamdeckplugininterface")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Rendering Options[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#rendering-options "Direct link to Rendering Options")

Implement **one** of the following four methods. If multiple are implemented, BTT uses the first one found in this order:

#### Option 1: Title Strings[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#option-1-title-strings "Direct link to Option 1: Title Strings")

Return an array of strings. BTT renders each string as a button with the user-configured appearance settings (background color, font, etc.).

    func widgetTitleStrings() -> [String]? {    return ["42%"]}

#### Option 2: Attributed Title Strings[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#option-2-attributed-title-strings "Direct link to Option 2: Attributed Title Strings")

Return attributed strings for custom text styling. BTT still applies additional user-configured styling (e.g. background color).

    func widgetAttributedTitleStrings() -> [NSAttributedString]? {    let attrs: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [        .font: NSFont.systemFont(ofSize: 20, weight: .bold),        .foregroundColor: NSColor.systemGreen    ]    return [NSAttributedString(string: "OK", attributes: attrs)]}

#### Option 3: Rendering Dictionaries[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#option-3-rendering-dictionaries "Direct link to Option 3: Rendering Dictionaries")

Return dictionaries with detailed rendering descriptions for full control over appearance including images, SF Symbols, colors, and corner radius.

    func widgetDictionaries() -> [[AnyHashable: Any]]? {    return [        [            "BTTStreamDeckBackgroundColor": "80, 96, 94, 255",            "BTTStreamDeckCornerRadius": 13,            "BTTStreamDeckSFSymbolName": "cpu",            "BTTStreamDeckSFSymbolStyle": 3,            "BTTStreamDeckIconColor1": "255, 255, 255, 255"        ]    ]}

**Available dictionary keys:**

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BTTStreamDeckBackgroundColor` | String | RGBA color string (e.g. `"80, 96, 94, 255"`) |
| `BTTStreamDeckCornerRadius` | Number | Corner radius in points |
| `BTTStreamDeckSFSymbolName` | String | SF Symbol name |
| `BTTStreamDeckSFSymbolStyle` | Number | SF Symbol rendering style |
| `BTTStreamDeckIconType` | Number | Icon type identifier |
| `BTTStreamDeckIconColor1` | String | Primary icon color (RGBA) |
| `BTTStreamDeckIconColor2` | String | Secondary icon color (RGBA) |
| `BTTStreamDeckIconColor3` | String | Tertiary icon color (RGBA) |
| `BTTStreamDeckImage` | String | Base64-encoded image data |
| `BTTStreamDeckImageReal` | NSImage | NSImage instance |
| `BTTStreamDeckImageWidth` | Number | Image width |
| `BTTStreamDeckImageHeight` | Number | Image height |
| `BTTStreamDeckImageOffsetX` | Number | Image horizontal offset |
| `BTTStreamDeckImageOffsetY` | Number | Image vertical offset |
| `BTTStreamDeckImageChangeColor` | Number | Whether to tint the image |
| `BTTStreamDeckResizeImage` | Number | Image resize mode |
| `BTTStreamDeckAttributedTitle` | String | Base64-encoded RTF attributed string |
| `BTTStreamDeckAttributedTitleReal` | NSAttributedString | NSAttributedString instance |
| `BTTStreamDeckAlternateImageHeight` | Number | Alternate image height |

#### Option 4: Pre-rendered Images[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#option-4-pre-rendered-images "Direct link to Option 4: Pre-rendered Images")

Return fully rendered `NSImage` instances. Images should be approximately 140x140 pixels - BTT resizes them to fit the specific device.

    func widgetImages() -> [NSImage]? {    let image = NSImage(size: NSSize(width: 140, height: 140))    image.lockFocus()    // ... custom drawing ...    image.unlockFocus()    return [image]}

### Button Handling[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#button-handling "Direct link to Button Handling")

Handle press and release events on Stream Deck buttons:

    // Called when the user presses the button. Return true to cancel assigned BTT actions.func buttonDown(_ identifier: String) -> Bool {    count += 1    delegate?.requestUpdate(self)    return false}// Called when the user releases the button. Return true to cancel assigned BTT actions.func buttonUp(_ identifier: String) -> Bool {    return false}

If your widget returns multiple buttons, implement `buttonIdentifiers()` with stable IDs in the same order and number as the rendered buttons:

    func buttonIdentifiers() -> [String]? {    return ["button1", "button2"]}

### Appearance Configuration[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#appearance-configuration "Direct link to Appearance Configuration")

Control whether appearance tabs are shown in BTT's configuration sidebar:

    // Show the standard appearance tab (background color, font, etc.)static func showAppearanceTab() -> Bool { return true }// Show the alternate appearance tabstatic func showAlternateAppearanceTab() -> Bool { return false }// Whether to use alternate appearance modefunc alternateModeActive() -> Bool { return false }

Return default appearance configuration values:

    static func defaultConfiguration() -> [AnyHashable: Any]? {    return [        "BTTStreamDeckCornerRadius": 13,        "BTTStreamDeckBackgroundColor": "40, 40, 40, 255"    ]}

### Delegate Methods[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#delegate-methods "Direct link to Delegate Methods")

The `delegate` property (type `BTTStreamDeckPluginDelegate`) provides:

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `executeAssignedBTTActions(_:)` | Execute the BTT actions assigned to this widget |
| `executeNamedTrigger(_:withReply:)` | Execute a named trigger configured in BTT |
| `executeScriptCommand(_:withParameters:asyncReply:)` | Execute a BTT script command |
| `requestUpdate(_:)` | Request BTT to re-render the widget |
| `setVariable(_:value:)` | Set a BTT variable |
| `getVariable(_:)` | Read a BTT variable |

### Requesting Updates[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#requesting-updates "Direct link to Requesting Updates")

Call `delegate?.requestUpdate(self)` whenever your widget's data changes and the display needs to refresh. BTT will then call your rendering method again.

    private func onDataChanged() {    delegate?.requestUpdate(self)}

Complete Example: CPU Core Count[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#complete-example-cpu-core-count "Direct link to Complete Example: CPU Core Count")

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This widget displays the number of active CPU cores. The configuration checkbox controls whether that count appears on the button.

    // BTT-Plugin-Name: System Monitor// BTT-Plugin-Identifier: com.example.systemmonitor// BTT-Plugin-Type: StreamDeck// BTT-Plugin-Icon: cpuimport Cocoaclass SystemMonitor: NSObject, BTTStreamDeckPluginInterface {    weak var delegate: (any BTTStreamDeckPluginDelegate)?    private var showCoreCount = true    static func configurationFormItems() -> BTTPluginFormItem? {        let group = BTTPluginFormItem()        group.formFieldType = BTTFormTypeFormGroup        let toggle = BTTPluginFormItem()        toggle.formFieldType = BTTFormTypeCheckbox        toggle.formLabel1 = "Show Core Count"        toggle.formFieldID = "showCoreCount"        toggle.defaultValue = NSNumber(value: true)        group.formOptions = [toggle]        return group    }    func didReceiveNewConfigurationValues(_ configurationValues: [AnyHashable: Any]) {        if let pct = configurationValues["plugin_var_showCoreCount"] as? Bool {            showCoreCount = pct        }        delegate?.requestUpdate(self)    }    func widgetTitleStrings() -> [String]? {        let info = ProcessInfo.processInfo        let usage = info.activeProcessorCount        if showCoreCount {            return ["CPU\n\(usage) cores"]        }        return ["CPU"]    }    func buttonDown(_ identifier: String) -> Bool {        return false    }    func buttonUp(_ identifier: String) -> Bool {        return false    }}

See the [CPU Usage Plugin on GitHub](https://github.com/folivoraAI/BetterTouchToolPlugins/tree/master/xcode-bundle-examples/BTTStreamDeckPluginCPUUsage)
 for the complete implementation with system-level CPU monitoring.

Xcode Bundle Setup[​](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#xcode-bundle-setup "Direct link to Xcode Bundle Setup")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For Xcode-based Stream Deck plugins, the bundle extension is `.bttstreamdeckplugin`. Set these `Info.plist` keys:

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `BTTPluginType` | `StreamDeck` |
| `NSPrincipalClass` | `$(PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME).YourClassName` |

See [Xcode Bundle Plugins & Distribution](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/xcode-bundle-distribution)
 for the full setup process.

*   [Protocol: `BTTStreamDeckPluginInterface`](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#protocol-bttstreamdeckplugininterface)
    *   [Rendering Options](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#rendering-options)
        
    *   [Button Handling](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#button-handling)
        
    *   [Appearance Configuration](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#appearance-configuration)
        
    *   [Delegate Methods](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#delegate-methods)
        
    *   [Requesting Updates](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#requesting-updates)
        
*   [Complete Example: CPU Core Count](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#complete-example-cpu-core-count)
    
*   [Xcode Bundle Setup](https://docs.folivora.ai/docs/plugins/stream-deck#xcode-bundle-setup)
